siva_et: 6.24 Abandoning without reserve all desires born of Sankalpa (thought and imagination) and completely restraining the whole group of the senses by the mind from all sides.
summary: Let go of the endless daydreams and cravings your mind cooks up, and gently reel your runaway senses back in.

siva_et: 6.25 Little by little let him attain to ietude by the intellect held firmly; having made the mind establish itself in the Self, let him not think of anything.
summary: Take it slow and steady. Step by step, quiet your mind with patience until it rests completely in your true self without wandering.

siva_et: 6.26 From whatever cause the restless and unsteady mind wanders away, from that let him restrain it and bring it under the control of the Self alone.
summary: Whenever your restless mind drifts off into anxiety or distraction, gently guide it back and anchor it firmly within yourself.

siva_et: 6.27 Supreme Bliss verily comes to this Yogi whose mind is ite peaceful, whose passion is ieted, who has become Brahman and who is free from sin.
summary: A deep, beautiful peace and overwhelming joy naturally come to those who quiet their passions and rest in pure awareness.

siva_et: 6.28 The Yogi, always engaging the mind thus (in the practice of Yoga), freed from sins, easily enjoys the Infinite Bliss of contact with Brahman (the Eternal).
summary: When you consistently quiet your mind and stay centered, you'll effortlessly experience a joyful, unbroken connection to the divine.

siva_et: 6.29 With the mind harmonised by Yoga he sees the Self abiding in all beings and all beings in the Self; he sees the same everywhere.
summary: When your mind is balanced, you begin to see the same divine spark in everyone around you, realizing we are all deeply connected.

siva_et: 6.30 He who sees Me everywhere and sees everything in Me, he never becomes separated from Me, nor do I become separated from him.
summary: When you see the divine in everything and everything in the divine, you'll never feel lost or separated from that loving presence again.

siva_et: 6.31 He who, being established in unity, worships Me Who dwells in all beings, that Yogi abides in Me, whatever may be his mode of living.
summary: No matter how you live your life, if you recognize the same divine essence dwelling in all beings, you are always living in tune with the divine.

siva_et: 6.32 He who, through the likeness of the Self, O Arjuna, sees eality everywhere, be it pleasure or pain, he is regarded as the highest Yogi.
summary: The highest spiritual state belongs to those who view everyone's joys and sorrows with a calm, compassionate, and steady heart.

siva_et: 6.33 Arjuna said  This Yoga of eanimity taught by Thee, O Krishna, I do not see its steady continuance, because of the restlessness (of the mind).
summary: Arjuna voices what we all feel: this path of total mental balance sounds wonderful, but my mind is just too restless and shaky to maintain it.

siva_et: 6.34 The mind verily is restless, turbulent, strong and unyielding, O Krishna: I deem it as difficult to control it as to control the wind.
summary: Arjuna voices a struggle we all know too well: our minds are stubborn, wild, and seemingly impossible to calm down.

siva_et: 6.35 The Blessed Lord said  Undoubtedly, O mighty-armed Arjuna, the mind is difficult to control and restless; but by practice and by dispassion it may be restrained.
summary: Krishna acknowledges how wild the mind is, but gently reassures you that it can be tamed through steady practice and learning to let go.

siva_et: 6.36 I think Yoga is hard to be attained by one of uncontrolled self, but the self-controlled and striving one can attain to it by the (proper) means.
summary: Finding inner calm can feel out of reach when we lack self-discipline, but with gentle persistence and the right approach, anyone can grow into it.

siva_et: 6.37 Arjuna said  He who is unable to control himself though he has the faith, and whose mind wanders away from Yoga, what end does he, having failed to attain perfection in Yoga, mee,t O Krishna?
summary: Arjuna asks a vulnerable question we often carry: if we have good intentions but keep stumbling and losing focus, what happens to us?

siva_et: Swami Sivananda did not comment on this sloka
summary: This verse is a transition space in the text, reflecting a moment of quiet pause in the dialogue.

siva_et: 6.39 This doubt of mine, O Krishna, do Thou dispel completely; because it is not possible for any but Thee to dispel this doubt.
summary: Arjuna turns to a trusted guide to completely clear away the heavy confusion weighing on his heart.

siva_et: 6.40 The Blessed Lord said  O Arjuna, neither in this world, nor in the next world is there destruction for him; none, verily, who does good, O My son, ever comes to grief.
summary: Take heart—Krishna promises that no sincere effort to do good is ever wasted, and you will never be truly ruined or lost.

siva_et: 6.41 Having attained to the worlds of the righteous and having dwelt there for everlasting years, he who fell from Yoga is rorn in a house of the pure and wealthy.
summary: Even if your spiritual journey gets interrupted, your progress isn't lost; you are safely held and will find support when you return.

siva_et: 6.42 Or he is born in a family of even the wise Yogis; verily a birth like this is very difficult to obtain in this world.
summary: Every step you take toward growth matters deeply, and you will eventually find yourself surrounded by the wisdom and support you need.

siva_et: 6.43 Thee he comes in touch with the knowledge acired in his former body and strives more than before for perfection, O Arjuna.
summary: The inner wisdom you worked so hard to build in the past stays with you, helping you pick up right where you left off and strive even harder.

siva_et: 6.44 By that very former practice he is borne on in spite of himself. Even he who merely wishes to know Yoga goes beyond the Brahmic word.
summary: Your past sincere efforts quietly carry you forward, gently pushing you past your old limits even when you feel stuck.

siva_et: 6.45 But the Yogi who strives with assiduity, purified of sins and perfected gradually through many births, reaches the highest goal.
summary: By patient, persistent effort over time, you gradually shed your burdens and naturally arrive at ultimate peace and fulfillment.

siva_et: 6.46 The Yogi is thought to be superior to the ascetics and even superior to men of knowledge (obtained through the study of scriptures); he is also superior to men of action; therefore be thou a Yogi, O Arjuna.
summary: Commitment from the heart goes far beyond just studying or strict discipline, so choose to dive fully into a path of connection and action.

siva_et: 6.47 And among all the Yogis he who, full of faith and with his inner self merged in Me, worships Me is deemed by Me to be the most devout.
summary: The most deeply centered and spiritually fulfilled person is the one who puts their whole heart and trust into the divine.

siva_et: 7.1 The Blessed Lord said  O Arjuna, hear how you shall without doubt know Me fully, with the mind intent on Me, practising Yoga and taking refuge in Me.
summary: Krishna invites you to quiet your mind, trust Him completely, and lean into a deeper practice to find true clarity.

siva_et: 7.2 I shall declare to thee in full this knowledge combined with realisation, after knowing which nothing more here remains to be known.
summary: He promises to share the ultimate truth with you—once you grasp it, you won't need to search anywhere else for meaning.

siva_et: 7.3 Among thousands of men, one perchance strives for perfection; even among those successful strivers, only one perchance knows Me in essence.
summary: The journey to deep self-realization takes dedication, and choosing to walk this path makes you truly rare.

siva_et: 7.4 Earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect and egoism  thus is My Nature divided eightfold.
summary: Everything tangible around us—from the earth to our own thoughts—makes up the physical expression of the divine.

siva_et: 7.5 This is the inferior Prakriti, O mighty-armed (Arjuna); know thou as different from it My higher Prakriti (Nature), the very life-element, by which this world is upheld.
summary: Beyond our physical bodies and daily stress lies a deeper, living spiritual energy that actually holds the universe together.

siva_et: 7.6 Know that these two (Natures) are the womb of all beings. So I am the source and dissolution of the whole universe.
summary: Everything in existence is born from and eventually returns to the divine source, which orchestrates the entire cycle of life.

siva_et: 7.7 There is nothing whatsoever higher than Me, O Arjuna. All this is strung on Me, as clusters of gems on a string.
summary: Just as a thread holds a necklace of gems together, the divine is the invisible support running through everything in your life.

siva_et: 7.8 I am the sapidity in water, O Arjuna; I am the light in the moon and the sun; I am the syllable Om in all the Vedas, sound in ether and virility in men.
summary: When you feel overwhelmed, remember that the beauty and energy in everyday things—like water, light, and sound—come straight from the divine.

siva_et: 7.9 I am the sweet fragrance in the earth and the brilliance in the fire, the life in all beings, and I am the austerity in ascetics.
summary: The very spark of life within you and the quiet strength you find in tough moments are expressions of a loving universe.

siva_et: 7.10 Know Me, O Arjuna, as the eternal seed of all beings; I am the intelligence of the intelligent; the splendour of the splendid objects am I.
summary: Whatever brilliance, sharp thinking, or potential you see in yourself or others is simply a reflection of the eternal source.

siva_et: 7.11 Of the strong, I am the strength devoid of desire and attachment, and in (all) beings, I am the desire unopposed to Dharma, O Arjuna.
summary: True strength isn't about grasping or forcing things; it's the healthy, wholesome drive to do what is right without selfish clinging.

siva_et: 7.12 Whatever beings (and objects) that are pure, active and inert, know that they proceed from Me. They are in Me, yet I am not in them.
summary: All of life's ups and downs come from the divine, yet the divine remains untouched and free from them—reminding you that you, too, can stay centered above your struggles.

siva_et: 7.13 Deluded by these Natures (states or things) composed of the three alities of Nature all this world does not know Me as distinct from them and immutable.
summary: It is easy to get caught up in the heavy drama of daily life and forget the timeless, unchanging reality that lies right beneath the surface.

siva_et: 7.14 Verily, this divine illusion of Mine, made up of the (three) alities (of Nature) is difficult to cross over; those who take refuge in Me alone, cross over this illusion.
summary: Life's illusions and heavy emotional traps can feel impossible to escape on your own, but letting go and leaning on the divine lifts that weight entirely.

siva_et: 7.15 The evil-doers and the deluded who are the lowest of men do not seek Me; they whose knowledge is destroyed by illusion follow the ways of demons.
summary: When we are trapped by our own negativity and self-delusion, we lose sight of what truly matters and drift into harmful habits.

siva_et: 7.16 Four kinds of virtuous men worship Me, O Arjuna, and they are the distressed, the seekr of knowledge, the seekr of wealth and the wise, O lord of the Bharatas.
summary: People turn to the divine for many reasons, whether they are hurting, searching for answers, looking for security, or simply seeking wisdom.

siva_et: 7.17 Of them the wise, ever steadfast and devoted to the One, excels (is the best); for I am exceedingly dear to the wise and he is dear to Me.
summary: The one who seeks truth with a steady heart shares a deeply loving, unbreakable bond with the divine.

siva_et: 7.18 Noble indeed are all these; but I deem the wise man as My very Self; for, steadfast in mind he is established in Me alone as the supreme goal.
summary: All sincere seekers are wonderful, but the wise soul who sees the divine as their ultimate home has truly arrived.

siva_et: 7.19 At the end of many births the wise man comes to Me, realising that all this is Vaasudeva (the innermost Self); such a great soul (Mahatma) is very hard to find.
summary: After a long journey of growing and learning, a rare soul finally realizes that the divine is everything and everywhere.

siva_et: 7.20 Those whose wisdom has been rent away by this or that desire, go to other gods, following this or that rite, led by their own nature.
summary: When we are blinded by specific cravings and intense desires, we often chase temporary fixes instead of lasting peace.

siva_et: 7.21 Whatsoever form any devotee desires to worship with faith  that (same) faith of his I make firm and unflinching.
summary: Whatever you put your genuine faith and heart into, the divine helps strengthen that devotion so you can keep going.

siva_et: 7.22 Endowed with that faith, he engages in the worship of that (form) and from it he obtains his desire, these being verily ordained by Me (alone).
summary: When you hold steady in your beliefs, you receive what you ask for, because the underlying order of the universe supports it.

siva_et: 7.23 Verily the reward (fruit) that accrues to those men of small intelligence is finite. The worshippers of the gods go to them, but My devotees come to Me.
summary: Chasing temporary rewards brings only fleeting satisfaction, while turning your heart toward the infinite brings boundless peace.

siva_et: 7.24 The foolish think of Me, the Unmanifest, as having manifestation, knowing not My higher, immutable and most excellent nature.
summary: It is easy to misunderstand the deeper reality of the divine when we only look at things through our limited human lens.

siva_et: 7.25 I am not manifest to all (as I am) veiled by the Yoga-Maya. This deluded world does not know Me, the unborn and imperishable.
summary: The ultimate truth is wrapped in layers of illusion, making it hard for most people to see the eternal reality right in front of them.

siva_et: 7.26 I know, O Arjuna, the beings of the past, the present and the future, but no one knows Me.
summary: Time holds no secrets from the divine, even if our human minds struggle to fully grasp the vastness of existence.

siva_et: 7.27 By the delusion of the pairs of opposites arising from desire and aversion, O Bharata, all beings are subject to delusion at birth, O Parantapa.
summary: We all get thrown off balance by the constant tug-of-war between likes and dislikes, joy and sorrow, right from the moment we are born.

siva_et: 7.28 But those men of virtuous deeds whose sins have come to an end, and who are freed from the delusion of the pairs of opposites, worship Me, steadfast in their vows.
summary: Those who let go of selfish habits and rise above the emotional roller coaster of life are finally free to devote their hearts fully to the divine.

siva_et: 7.29 Those who strive for liberation from old age and death, taking refuge in Me, realise in full ï1thatï1 Brahman, the whole knowledge of the Self and all action.
summary: When you turn to the divine for refuge, you slowly come to understand your true spiritual nature and the deepest truths of existence.

siva_et: 7.30 Those who know Me with the Adhibhuta (pertaining to the elements), Adhidaiva (pertaining to the gods) and the Adhiyajna (pertaining to the sacrifice) know Me even at the time of death, steadfast in mind.
summary: Those who keep their hearts anchored in the divine stay steady and at peace, even in their final moments.

siva_et: Swami Sivananda did not comment on this sloka
summary: This verse serves as a transition or introductory marker without commentary, setting the stage for Arjuna's next questions.

siva_et: 8.2 Who and how is Adhiyajna here in this body, O destroyer of Madhu (Krishna)? And how at the time of death, art Thou to be known by the self-controlled?
summary: Arjuna asks the ultimate question of how a person can remain centered and conscious of the divine when the end of life arrives.

siva_et: 8.3 The Blessed Lord said  Brahman is the Imperishable, the Supreme; Its essential nature is called Self-knowledge; the offering (to the gods) which causes existence and manifestation of beings and which also sustains them is called action.
summary: The divine explains the foundational reality of existence: an unchanging supreme spirit that gives life to all things.

siva_et: 8.4 Adhibhuta (knowledge of the elements) pertains to My perishable Nature and the Purusha or the Soul is the Adhidaiva; I alone am the Adhiyajna here in this body, O best among the embodied (men).
summary: Everything in the material and spiritual world is interconnected, and the divine presence resides directly within your own body.

siva_et: 8.5 And whosoever, leaving the body, goes forth remembering Me alone, at the time of death, he attains My Being: there is no doubt about this.
summary: Whatever state of mind you hold onto as you leave this life is where your consciousness naturally flows, so anchor yourself in the divine.

siva_et: 8.6 Whosoever at the end leaves the body, thinking of any being, to that being only does he go, O son of Kunti (Arjuna), because of his constant thought of that being.
summary: Your final thoughts and attachments shape your transition, as the mind tends to drift toward whatever it has obsessed over during life.

siva_et: 8.7 Therefore at all times remember Me only and fight. With mind and intellect fixed (or absorbed) in Me, thou shalt doubtessly come to Me alone.
summary: Go ahead and handle your responsibilities in life, but keep your heart and mind constantly connected to the divine.

siva_et: 8.8 With the mind not moving towards any other thing, made steadfast by the method of habitual meditation, and constantly meditating, one goes to the Supreme Person, the Resplendent, O Arjuna.
summary: Through patient, steady practice, you can train your restless mind to stop wandering and finally rest in the supreme light.

siva_et: 8.9 Whosoever meditates on the Omniscient, the Ancient, the Ruler (of the whole world), minuter than an atom, the supporter of all, of inconceivable form, effulgent like the sun and beyond the darkness of ignorance.
summary: Meditate on the supreme cosmic presence—the wise, radiant supporter of all creation who shines far beyond the darkness of ignorance.

siva_et: 8.10 At the time of death, with unshaken mind, endowed with devotio, by the power of Yoga, fixing the whole life-breath in the middle of the two eyrows, he reaches that resplendent Supreme Person.
summary: By practicing deep concentration and keeping your mind devoted and unshaken at the end, you reach the highest divine state.

siva_et: 8.11 That which is declared Imperishable by those who know the Vedas, that which the self-controlled (ascetics or Sannyasins) and passion-free enter, that desiring which celibacy is practised  that goal I will declare to thee in brief.
summary: The supreme, eternal goal is found by those who conquer their passions and live with a focused, disciplined heart.

siva_et: 8.12 Having closed all the gates, confined the mind in the heart and fixed the life-breath in the head, engaged in the practice of concentration.
summary: By pulling your awareness away from external distractions and centering your life-breath within, you can enter deep, meditative focus.

siva_et: 8.13 Uttering the one-syllabled Om  the Brahman  and remembering Me, he who departs, leaving the body, attains to the Supreme Goal.
summary: When it's your time to leave this life, holding the Divine in your heart and mind will guide you to ultimate peace.

siva_et: 8.14 I am easily attainable by that ever-steadfast Yogi who constantly and daily remembers Me (for a long time), not thinking of anything else (with a single mind or one-pointed mind), O Partha (Arjuna).
summary: Keep your heart fixed on the Divine with quiet, daily devotion, and you will feel an unbreakable connection that is always within reach.

siva_et:
8.15 Having attained Me these great souls do not again take birth (here) which is the place of pain 
and is non-eternal: they have reached the highest perfection (liberation).
summary: Life here can feel painful and fleeting, but once you truly find your way home to the Divine, your search is over and your heart is at rest.

siva_et: 8.16 (All) the worlds including the world of Brahma are subject to return again, O Arjuna; but he who reaches Me, O son of Kunti, has no rirth.
summary: Every worldly comfort and achievement will eventually fade, but finding refuge in the Divine takes you beyond the endless cycle of struggle.

siva_et: 8.17 Those people who know the day of Brahma which is of a duration of a thousand Yugas (ages) and the night which is also of a thousand Yugas duration, they know day and night.
summary: There is a vast, timeless rhythm to the universe that stretches far beyond our human comprehension of time.

siva_et: 8.18 From the Unmanifested all the manifested (worlds) proceed at the coming of the 'day'; at the coming of the 'night' they dissolve verily into ï1thatï1 alone which is called the Unmanifested.
summary: Everything in the physical universe shifts and changes—manifesting into life and then resting quietly back into the unseen source.

siva_et: 8.19 This same multitude of beings, being born again and again, is dissolved, helplessly, O Arjuna (into the Unmanifested) at the coming of the night and comes forth at the coming of the day.
summary: Caught in the changing tides of time, living things rise and return to the earth over and over until they find a deeper freedom.

siva_et: 8.20 But verily there exists, higher than this Unmanifested, another unmanifested Eternal, which is not destroyed when all beings are destroyed.
summary: Far beyond this changing, temporary world lies an eternal reality that remains untouched even when everything else falls away.

siva_et: 8.21 What is called the Unmanifested and the Imperishable, That they say is the highest goal. They who reach It do not return (to this Samsara). That is My highest abode (place or state).
summary: That unchanging, highest realm is your ultimate destination; once you reach it, you never have to wander through pain and confusion again.

siva_et: 8.22 That highest Purusha, O Arjuna, is attainable by unswerving devotion to Him alone within Whom all beings dwell and by Whom all this is pervaded.
summary: The Supreme Being—who holds all things within Himself—can only be reached through a heart full of deep, unwavering love and surrender.

siva_et: 8.23 Now I will tell thee, O chief of Bharatas, the times departing at which the Yogis will return or not return.
summary: Now, let's explore the spiritual paths and departures that lead either back into this world or onward to ultimate liberation.

siva_et: 8.24 Fire, light daytime, the bright fortnight, the six months of the northern path of the sun (the northern solstice)  departing then (by these) men who know Brahman go to Brahman.
summary: Those who walk in the light of truth and spiritual awakening ultimately journey straight to the eternal Divine.

siva_et: 8.25 Attaining to the lunar light by smoke, night time, the dark fortnight also, the six months of the southern path of the sun (the southern solstice), the Yogi returns.
summary: Those focused on worldly rewards and temporary light will eventually return to experience life in this earthly realm once more.

siva_et: 8.26 The bright and the dark paths of the world are verily thought to be eternal; by the one (the bright path) a man goes not to return and by the other (the dark path) he returns.
summary: There are two eternal paths: one leads you out of the cycle of rebirth into freedom, while the other pulls you back into earthly life.

siva_et: 8.27 Knowing these paths, O Arjuna, no Yogi is deluded; therefore at all times be steadfast in Yoga.
summary: When you understand the deeper truths of life, you won't get easily lost or confused. Stay anchored in your spiritual practice no matter what comes your way.

siva_et: 8.28 Whatever fruit of merit is declared (in the scriptures) to accrue from (the study of) the Vedas, (the performance of) sacrifices, (the practice of) austerities, and gifts  beyond all this goes the Yogi, having known this; and he attains to the Supreme Primeval (first or ancient) Abode.
summary: Going beyond ordinary rituals and good deeds leads you to the ultimate peace of the Divine. By truly connecting with the sacred within, you reach a timeless home.

siva_et: 9.1 The Blessed Lord said  I shall now declare to thee who does not cavil, the greatest secret, the knowledge combined with experience (Self-realisation). Having known this thou shalt be free evil.
summary: When you approach life with an open and trusting heart, profound wisdom is unlocked for you. This deep self-knowledge helps lift the heavy burdens of pain and struggle.

siva_et: 9.2 This is the kingl science, the kingly secret, the supreme purifier, realisable by direct intuitional knowledge, according to righteousness, very easy to perform and imperishable.
summary: This path of wisdom is the greatest of all because it directly purifies the heart and is surprisingly natural to follow. It brings an everlasting peace that you can feel for yourself.

siva_et: 9.3 Those who have no faith in this Dharma (knowledge of the Self), O Parantapa (Arjuna), return to the path of this world of death without attaining Me.
summary: When we struggle to trust a higher purpose or our deeper self, we tend to stay trapped in endless cycles of struggle and suffering. Faith is the bridge that helps us break free.

siva_et: 9.4 All this world is pervaded by Me in My unmanifest aspect; all beings exist in Me, but I do not dwell in them.
summary: The Divine quietly permeates every corner of the universe, holding everything together from behind the scenes. Even when you feel alone, you are resting within a loving presence.

siva_et: 9.5 Nor do beings exist in Me (in reality); behold My divine Yoga, supporting all beings, but not dwelling in them, is My Self, the efficient cause of beings.
summary: There is a profound mystery to how life is sustained, existing beyond our ordinary understanding. You are deeply supported by a universal power that remains completely free.

siva_et: 9.6 As the mighty wind, moving everywhere, rests always in the ether, even so, know thou that all beings rest in Me.
summary: Just as the wind moves freely within the vast sky, everything in existence rests safely within the divine embrace. You too are held by something much larger than your worries.

siva_et: 9.7 All beings, O Arjuna, go into My Nature at the end of a Kalpa; I send them forth again at the beginning of (the next) Kalpa.
summary: Cycles of beginning and ending are natural parts of the grand cosmic design. Nothing is ever truly lost, as everything rests and re-emerges in its own time.

siva_et: 9.8 Animating My Nature, I again and again send forth all this multitude of beings, helpless by the force of the Nature.
summary: Life often feels like it's spinning on its own automatic, overwhelming momentum, pushing us along. Yet behind these repeating patterns, there is a greater unfolding at play.

siva_et: 9.9 These acts do not bind Me, O Arjuna, sitting like one indifferent, unattached to those acts.
summary: True freedom means being involved in life's actions without being chained down by their outcomes. You can learn to remain peaceful and centered, even amidst busy circumstances.

siva_et: 9.10 Under Me as supervisor, Nature produces the moving and the unmoving; because of this, O Arjuna, the world revolves.
summary: There is an intelligent rhythm operating behind all of nature's movements and changes. Even when life feels chaotic, it is unfolding under a steady, watchful presence.

siva_et: 9.11 Fools disregard Me, clad in human form, not knowing My higher Being as the great Lord of (all) beings.
summary: It's easy to overlook the sacredness in everyday life when we get caught up in superficial appearances. Look past the surface to recognize the deeper divine reality in and around you.

siva_et: 9.12 Of vain hopes, of vain actions, of vain knowledge and senseless, they verily are possessed of the deceitful nature of demons and undivine beings.
summary: When our hopes and efforts are driven purely by ego and confusion, we end up feeling empty and frustrated. True fulfillment eludes us until we drop our resistance and align with something higher.

siva_et: 9.13 But the great souls, O Arjuna, partaking of My divine nature, worship Me with a single mind (with the mind devoted to nothing else), knowing Me as the imperishable source of beings.
summary: Great souls find deep refuge by turning their whole heart toward the Divine, recognizing it as the timeless source of all life.

siva_et: 9.14 Always glorifying Me, striving,firm in vows, prostrating themselves before Me, they worship Me with devotion always steadfast.
summary: When you commit your daily efforts and steady devotion to something greater, your heart naturally finds an anchor of peace.

siva_et: 9.15 Others also sacrificing with the wisdom-sacrifice worship Me, the All-faced, as one, as distinct, and as manifold.
summary: People connect with the Divine in many different ways—some through quiet wisdom, others through devotion—yet all paths lead to the same ultimate truth.

siva_et: 9.16 I am the Kratu; I am the Yajna; I am the offering (food) to the manes; I am the medicinal herbs and all the plants; I am the Mantra; I am also the Ghee or the melted butter; I am the fire; I am the oblation.
summary: The sacred and the everyday are not separate; the Divine is woven into every ritual, nourishment, and action of your life.

siva_et:
9.17 I am the father of this world, the mother, the dispenser of the fruits of actions and the 
grandfather; the (one) thing to be known, the purifier, the sacred monosyllable (Om), and also the Rik-, the Sama-and the Yajur-Vedas.
summary: You are never truly alone, because the Divine is the mother, father, and ultimate guide of your entire journey.

siva_et: 9.18 I am the goal, the supporter, the Lord, the witness, the abode, the shelter, the friend, the origin, the dissolution, the foundation, the treasure-house and the seed which is imperishable.
summary: In times of uncertainty, remember that you are sustained by a compassionate presence that serves as your truest home, refuge, and friend.

siva_et: 9.19 (As the sun) I give heat; I withhold and send forth the rain; I am immortality and also death, existence and non-existence, O Arjuna.
summary: Both the challenges and blessings of life—and even life and death themselves—are expressions of one vast, unified reality.

siva_et: 9.20 The knowers of the three Vedas, the drinkers of Soma, purified of all sins, worshipping Me by sacrifices, pray for the way to heaven; they reach the holy world of the Lord of the gods and enjoy in heavn the divine pleasures of the gods.
summary: Seeking temporary rewards and pleasures can bring fleeting happiness, but it keeps you caught in a cycle of wanting.

siva_et: 9.21 They, having enjoyed the vast heaven, enter the world of mortals when their merit is exhausted; thus abiding by the injunctions of the ï1threeï1 (Vedas) and desiring (objects of) desires, they attain to the state of going and returning.
summary: Chasing external rewards only offers temporary satisfaction before bringing you right back to where you started; true peace lies beyond endless craving.

siva_et: 9.22 For those men who worship Me alone, thinking of no other, for those ever-united, I secure what is not already possessed and preserve what they already possess.
summary: When you quiet your mind and dedicate your heart entirely to the Divine, your deepest needs and security are lovingly cared for.

siva_et: 9.23 Even those devotees who, endowed with faith, worship other gods, worship Me alone, O Arjuna, b the wrong method.
summary: Whatever or however you worship with a sincere heart, your devotion ultimately reaches the one supreme source of all.

siva_et: 9.24 (For) I alone am the enjoyer and also the Lord of all sacrifices; but they do not know Me in essence (in reality), and hence they fall (return to this mortal world).
summary: Recognizing the divine presence behind all your efforts frees you from getting stuck in endless, exhausting cycles.

siva_et: 9.25 The worshippers of the gods go to them; to the manes go the ancestor-worshippers; to the deities who preside over the elements go their worshippers; but My devotees come to Me.
summary: Whatever you set your heart on—whether temporary goals or lasting peace—is ultimately where your journey leads.

siva_et: 9.26 Whoever offers Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or a little water  that, so offered devotedly by the pure-minded, I accept.
summary: It is not the size or grandness of your offering that matters, but the pure, loving intent of your heart, which is always welcomed.

siva_et: 9.27 Whatever thou doest, whatever thou eatest, whatever thou offerest in sacrifice, whatever thou givest, whatever thou practisest as austerity, O Arjuna, do it as an offering unto Me.
summary: Turn your daily actions, meals, and efforts into a loving offering to the divine. When you let go of needing personal credit, your everyday life becomes a sacred practice.

siva_et: 9.28 Thus shalt thou be freed from the bonds of actions yielding good and evil fruits; with the mind steadfast in the Yoga of renunciation, and liberated, thou shalt come unto Me.
summary: By releasing your heavy attachment to the results of your actions, you free yourself from anxiety and find true liberation.

siva_et: 9.29 The same am I to all beings; to Me there is none hateful or dear; but those who worship Me with devotion are in Me and I am also in them.
summary: The divine loves everyone equally and plays no favorites. If you lean into that loving connection with an open heart, you will feel a deep, unbreakable closeness.

siva_et: 9.30 Even if the most sinful worships Me, with devotion to none else, he too should indeed by regarded as righteous for he has rightly resolved.
summary: No matter how many mistakes you have made or how far you have strayed, a sincere turn toward the good puts you back on the right path.

siva_et: 9.31 Soon he becomes righteous and attains to eternal peace; O Arjuna, proclaim thou for certain that My devotee never perishes.
summary: When your heart is truly devoted, your inner turmoil settles into lasting peace. Rest easy knowing that those who seek the divine are fiercely protected.

siva_et: 9.32 For, taking refuge in Me, they also who, O Arjuna, may be of a sinful birth  women, Vaisyas as well as Sudras  attain the Supreme Goal.
summary: No matter your background, status, or past, turning to the divine opens the door to ultimate peace and freedom for everyone.

siva_et: 9.33 How much more (easily) then the hold Brahmins and devoted royal saints (attain the goal); having come to this impermanent and unhappy world, do thou worship Me.
summary: This world can be a painful and fleeting place, so give your heart to something higher. Focusing your devotion here brings ultimate meaning to a difficult journey.

siva_et: 9.34 Fix thy mind on Me; by devoted to Me; sacrifice unto Me; bow down to Me; having thus united thy whole self to Me, taking Me as the supreme goal, thou shalt come unto Me.
summary: Keep your mind and heart completely anchored in the divine as your ultimate goal. By dedicating your whole self to this presence, you will find your way home.

siva_et: 10.1 The Blessed Lord said  Again, O mighty-armed Arjuna, listen to my supreme word which I will declare to thee who who art beloved, for thy welfare.
summary: Listen closely to these comforting words meant to bring you deep personal well-being and strength. You are cared for and guided.

siva_et: 10.2 Neither the hosts of the gods nor the great sages know My origin; for in every way I am the source of all the gods and the great sages.
summary: The ultimate source of everything in the universe is vast and beyond human comprehension. Everything you see originates from this singular, timeless root.

siva_et: 10.3 He who knows Me as unborn and beginningless, as the great Lord of the worlds, he, among mortals, is undeluded and he is liberated from all sins.
summary: When you truly understand that the divine is eternal and the master of all, your confusion clears and your heavy burdens lift.

siva_et: 10.4 Intellect, wisdom, non-delusion, forgiveness, truth, self-restraint, calmness, happiness, pain, existence or birth, non-existence or death, fear and also fearlessness.
summary: Every human experience—from intellect and forgiveness to pain, fear, and courage—flows from a single source. All of it is part of the divine tapestry of life.

siva_et: 10.5 Non-injury, eanimity, contentment, austerity, beneficence, fame, ill-fame  (these) different kinds of alities of beings arise from Me alone.
summary: Compassion, contentment, inner balance, and the courage to endure all spring from the divine. Cultivating these qualities brings you closer to your true nature.

siva_et: 10.6 The seven great sages, the ancient four and also the Manus, possessed of powers like Me (on account of their minds being fixed on Me), were born of (My) mind; from them are these creatures born in this world.
summary: The ancient sages and ancestors who shaped the wisdom of our world all arose from a single divine source of consciousness.

siva_et: 10.7 He who in truth knows these manifold manifestations of My Being and (this) Yoga-power of Mine becomes established in the unshakable Yoga; there is no doubt about it.
summary: When you truly understand the divine presence working in and around you, your mind settles into an unshakeable inner peace.

siva_et: 10.8 I am the source of all; from Me everything evolves; understanding thus, the wise, endowed with meditation, worship Me.
summary: Recognizing the source of all life brings a deep sense of meaning, turning your daily reflection into a heartfelt worship.

siva_et: 10.9 With their mind and their life wholly absorbed in Me, enlightening each other and ever speaking of Me, they are satisfied and delighted.
summary: True fulfillment comes when you surround yourself with others who share your spiritual focus, finding deep joy in uplifting conversations.

siva_et: 10.10 To them who are ever steadfast, worshipping Me with love, I give the Yoga of discrimination by which they come to Me.
summary: When you approach life with a loving and steady heart, clarity and wisdom are naturally given to guide your way.

siva_et: 10.11 Out of mere compassion for them, I, dwelling within their Self, destroy the darkness born of ignorance by the luminous lamp of knowledge.
summary: Out of deep love for you, the divine light within clears away the darkness of confusion and ignorance.

siva_et: 10.12 Arjuna said  Thou art the Supreme Brahman, the supreme abode (or the supreme light), the supreme purifier, eternal, divine Person, the primeval God, unborn andn omnipresent.
summary: Arjuna praises the ultimate, eternal source of all existence as the supreme light and purifier of the soul.

siva_et: 10.13 All the sages have thus declared Thee, as also the divine sage Narada; so also Asita, Devala and Vyasa; and now Thou Thyself sayest so to me.
summary: All the great sages and enlightened teachers throughout history have confirmed these profound truths, and now you hear them directly.

siva_et: 10.14 I believe all this that Thou sayest to me to be true, O Krishna; verily, O blessed Lord! neither the gods nor the demons know Thy manifestation (origin).
summary: Arjuna expresses complete trust in Krishna's words, acknowledging that the true depth of the divine is beyond ordinary human or cosmic comprehension.

siva_et: Swami Sivananda did not comment on this sloka
summary: This verse has no commentary provided, but it sits within the sacred dialogue of recognizing divine greatness.

siva_et: 10.16 Thou shouldst indeed tell, without reserve, of Thy divine glories by which Thou existest, pervading all these worlds. (None else can do so.)
summary: Arjuna asks to hear more about the magnificent ways the divine presence infuses and sustains every corner of the universe.

siva_et:
10.17 How shall I, ever meditating, know Thee, O Yogin? In what aspects or things, O blessed 
Lord, art Thou to be thought of by me?
summary: Arjuna wonders how to constantly keep his mind focused on the divine, asking where and in what forms he should look for that presence.

siva_et: 10.18 Tell me again in detail, O Krishna, of Thy Yogic power and glory; for I am not satiated with what I have heard of Thy life-giving and nectar-like speech.
summary: Thirsting for more wisdom, Arjuna asks to hear in detail about divine power because these uplifting words bring him deep nourishment.

siva_et: 10.19 The Blessed Lord said  Very well! Now I will declare to thee My divine glories in their prominence, O Arjuna; there is no end to their detailed description.
summary: The Lord agrees to share the most prominent expressions of divine majesty, though they are ultimately infinite and endless.

siva_et: 10.20 I am the Self, O Gudakesa, seated in the hearts of all beings; I am the beginning, the middle and also the end of all beings.
summary: Deep within your heart resides the true Self, which forms the very beginning, middle, and end of all existence.

siva_et: 10.21 Among the (twelve) Adityas, I am Vishnu; among luminaries, the radiant sun; I am Marichi among the (seven or forty-nine) Maruts; among stars the moon am I.
summary: Krishna reminds us that the brightest, most magnificent wonders in the universe are simply reflections of His divine presence.

siva_et: 10.22 Among the Vedas I am the Sama-Veda; I am Vasava among the gods; among the senses I am the mind; and I am intelligence among living beings.
summary: When you look at your own mind and deep intelligence, recognize that this brilliant spark within you is a direct expression of the Divine.

siva_et: 10.23 And, among the Rudras I am Sankara; among the Yakshas and Rakshasas, the Lord of wealth (Kubera); among the Vasus I am Pavaka (fire); and among the (seven) mountains I am the Meru.
summary: Even the greatest symbols of earthly wealth and fierce power carry the sacred energy of Krishna's majesty.

siva_et:
10.24 And, among the household priests (of kings), O Arjuna, know Me to be the chief, Brihaspati; among the army generals I am Skana; among lakes I am the ocean.
'
summary: Whenever you witness supreme leadership or the vast, untamed depths of the ocean, know that the Divine is at the heart of it.

siva_et: 10.25 Among the great sages I am Bhrigu; among words I am the one syllable (Om); among sacrifices I am the sacrifice of silent repetition; among the immovable things I am the Himalayas.
summary: In quiet moments of silent prayer and steady meditation, you are connecting directly with the unshakeable presence of the Divine.

siva_et: 10.26 Among all the trees ( I am) the Peepul; among the divine sages, I am Narada; among Gandharvas, Chitraratha; among the perfected, the sage Kapila.
summary: Among the wonders of nature and the wisest souls, the Divine shines through as the ultimate source of grace and perfection.

siva_et: 10.27 Know Me as Ucchaisravas born of nectar, among horses; among lordly elephants (I am) the Airavata; and, among men, the king.
summary: The majesty found in noble creatures and true leaders are earthly mirrors of Krishna's boundless glory.

siva_et: 10.28 Among weapons I am the thunderbolt; among cows I am the wish-fulfilling cow called Kamadhenu; I am the progenitor, the god of love; among serpents I am Vasuki.
summary: From forces of intense power to the deepest passions of the heart, all of creation draws its life force from the Divine.

siva_et: 10.29 I am Ananta among the Nagas; I am Varuna among water-deities; Aryaman among the Manes I am; I am Yama among the governors.
summary: Even the stern forces of justice, water, and ultimate order are simply different faces of the same loving Source.

siva_et: 10.30 And, I am Prahlada among the demons, among the reckoners I am time; among beasts I am the lion, and Vainateya (Garuda) among birds.
summary: Time that keeps moving forward and the fierce courage found in the natural world are reminders of Krishna's unstoppable power.

siva_et: 10.31 Among the purifiers (or the speeders) I am the wind; Rama among the warriors am I; among the fishes I am the shark; among the streams I am the Ganga.
summary: In the rushing winds, the mighty rivers, and the warriors of integrity, the Divine flows as the ultimate purifier.

siva_et: 10.32 Among creations I am the beginning, the middle and also the end, O Arjuna; among the sciences I am the science of the Self; and I am the logic among controversialists.
summary: Krishna is the beginning, middle, and end of everything, reminding us that understanding our true Self is the highest knowledge.

siva_et:
10.33 Among the letters of the alphabets, the letter 'A' I am and the dual among the compounds. I am verily the inexhaustible or everlasting time; I am the dispenser (of the fruits of actions) having 
faces in all directions.
summary: As timeless time itself and the very foundation of language, the Divine orchestrates the unfolding of every action and its result.

siva_et: 10.34 And I am the all-devouring Death, and the prosperity of those who are to be prosperous; among the feminine alities (I am) fame, prosperity, speech, memory, intelligence, firmness and forgiveness.
summary: Life's great successes, enduring virtues, and even the reality of death are all manifestations of the all-encompassing Divine.

siva_et: 10.35 Among the hymns also I am the Brihatsaman; among metres Gayatri am I; among the montsh I am the Margasirsha; among the seasons (I am) the flowery season.
summary: The divine presence fills the finest and most sacred elements of the natural and spiritual worlds.

siva_et: 10.36 I am the gambling of the fraudulent; I am the splendour of the splendid; I am victory; I am determination (of those who are determined); I am the goodness of the good.
summary: God is the underlying essence behind everything—from human determination and victory to the very qualities of goodness and strength.

siva_et: 10.37 Among the Vrishnis I am Vaasudeva; among the Pandavas I am Arjuna; among the sages I am Vyasa; among the Poets I am Usanas, the poet.
summary: In every great lineage, sage, and visionary, the divine essence shines forth as the supreme representative.

siva_et: 10.38 Of those who punish, I am the sceptre; among those who seek victory, I am statesmanship; and also among secrets, I am silence; knowledge among knowers I am.
summary: The sacred quiet of silence and the wisdom of those who know represent the profound depth of the divine.

siva_et: 10.39 And whatever is the seed of all beings, that also am I, O Arjuna; there is no being, whether moving or unmoving, that can exist without Me.
summary: Nothing in this entire universe, living or unmoving, could exist for a single moment without the divine seed that sustains it all.

siva_et: 10.40 There is no end to My divine gloreis, O Arjuna, but this is a brief statement by Me of the particulars of My divine glories.
summary: The wondrous glories of the divine are limitless, and these examples are merely a glimpse into an infinite majesty.

siva_et: 10.41 Whatever being there is glorious, prosperous or powerful, that know thou to be a manifestation of a part of My splendour.
summary: Whenever you witness true glory, prosperity, or power, know that it is simply a tiny spark of the divine's overwhelming splendor.

siva_et: 10.42 But, of what avail to thee is the knowledge of all these details, O Arjuna? I exist, supporting this whole world by one part of Myself.
summary: There is no need to get lost in endless details, because the entire universe is simply held and sustained by a single fraction of the divine.

siva_et: 11.1 Arjuna said  By this word (explanation) of the highest secret concerning the Self which Thou hast spoken, for the sake of blessing me, my delusion is gone.
summary: When your heart truly grasps higher spiritual truths, the fog of confusion and delusion naturally lifts away.

siva_et: 11.2 The origin and the destruction of beings verily have been heard by me in detail from Thee, O lotus-eyed Lord, and also Thy inexhaustible greatness.
summary: Understanding where we come from and where we go helps us appreciate the limitless greatness of the divine.

siva_et: 11.3 (Now) O Supreme Lord, as Thou hast thus described Thyself, O Supreme Person, I wish to see Thy divine form.
summary: When you feel ready to go deeper, a sincere yearning awakens within you to directly experience the vast, divine reality.

siva_et: 11.4 If Thou, O Lord, thinkest it possible for me to see it, do Thou, then, O Lord of the Yogins, show me Thy imperishable Self.
summary: With a humble heart, you can ask for the strength and grace to witness the higher, imperishable truth of existence.

siva_et: 11.5 The Blessed Lord said  Behold, O Arjuna, forms of Mine, by the hundreds and thousands, of different sorts, divine, and of various colours and shapes.
summary: The divine invites you to open your eyes to an infinite, breathtaking array of forms and wonders beyond human imagination.

siva_et: 11.6 Behold the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Asvins and also the Maruts; behold many wonders never seen before, O Arjuna.
summary: Behold the magnificent forces of the universe and countless marvels you never knew existed, all unfolding in divine harmony.

siva_et: 11.7 Now behold, O Arjuna, in this, My body, the whole universe centred in one  including the moving and the unmoving  and whatever else thou desirest to see.
summary: Krishna invites you to see the entire vast universe contained right within Him, revealing a reality far beyond your immediate worries.

siva_et: 11.8 But thou art not able to behold Me with these thine own eyes; I give thee the divine eye; behold My lordly Yoga.
summary: Sometimes our ordinary vision is too limited to see the divine working in our lives, but grace can open our eyes to a deeper truth.

siva_et: 11.9 Sanjaya said  Having thus spoken, O king, the great Lord of Yoga, hari (Krishna), showed to Arjuna His supreme form as the Lord.
summary: In moments of great revelation, the divine grandeur is unveiled, reminding us that a higher power is always active and present.

siva_et: 11.10 With numerous mouths and eyes, with numerous wonderful sights, with numerous divine ornaments, with numerous divine weapons uplifted (such a form He showed).
summary: The true scale of the universe can feel overwhelming and awe-inspiring when we finally catch a glimpse of its infinite complexity.

siva_et: 11.11 Wearing divine garlands (necklaces) and apparel, anointed with divine unguents, the all-wonderful, resplendent (Being) endless with faces on all sides.
summary: Beyond our everyday struggles lies a brilliant, radiant reality that encompasses everything in existence with boundless beauty.

siva_et: 11.12 If the splendour of a thousand suns were to blaze out at once (simultaneously) in the sky, that would be the splendour of that mighty Being (great Soul).
summary: The sheer power of the divine is blindingly bright, reminding us how small our personal dramas are in the presence of ultimate majesty.

siva_et: 11.13 There, in the body of the God of gods, Arjuna then saw the whole universe resting in one, with its many groups.
summary: Everything in creation rests securely within the heart of the divine, connected and held together by a single source.

siva_et: 11.14 Then, Arjuna, filled with wonder and with his hair standing on end, bowed down his head to the God and spoke with joined palms.
summary: When faced with the sheer wonder of existence, our ego naturally melts away into deep humility, reverence, and surrender.

siva_et: 11.15 Arjuna said  I see all the gods, O God, in Thy body, and (also) hosts of various classes of beings, Brahma, the Lord, seated on the lotus, all the sages and the celestial serpents.
summary: Arjuna looks into the divine form and sees every aspect of life and consciousness united as one harmonious whole.

siva_et: 11.16 I see Thee of boundless form on every side with many arms, stomachs, mouths and eyes: neither the end nor the middle nor also the beginning do I see, O Lord of the universe, O Cosmic Form.
summary: When we look closely at the universe, we see it has no beginning or end—it is an infinite, living presence that surrounds us completely.

siva_et:
11.17 I see Thee with the diadem, the club and the discus, a mass of radiance shining 
everywhere, very hard to look at, blazing all round like burning fire and the sun, and immeasurable.
summary: The blazing, radiant energy of the divine can feel intense and terrifying to look upon, demanding our absolute awe.

siva_et: 11.18 Thou art the Imperishable, the Supreme Being, worthy to be known. Thou art the great treasure-house of this universe; Thou art the imperishable protector of the eternal Dhrama; Thou art the Primal Person, I deem.
summary: You are looking at the ultimate, unchanging truth of the universe—the eternal protector and timeless source of all that is good.

siva_et: 11.19 I see Thee without beginning, middle or end, infinite in power, of endless arms, the sun and the moon being Thy eyes, the burning fire Thy mouth, heating the whole universe with Thy radiance.
summary: The divine presence is infinitely powerful and all-pervading, warming and energizing every corner of existence with its radiant light.

siva_et: 11.20 This space between the earth and the heaven and all the arters are filled by Thee alone; having seen this, Thy wonderful and teriible form, the three worlds are trembling with fear, O great-souled Being.
summary: Witnessing the raw, unfiltered power of the cosmos can make us tremble, shaking us out of our petty concerns into a state of profound awe.

siva_et: 11.21 Verily, into Thee enter these hosts of gods; some extol Thee in fear with joined palms; saying 'may it be well', bands of great sages and perfected ones praise Thee with hymns complete.
summary: Even the greatest divine beings and sages look to the cosmic power with awe, prayer, and a deep longing for well-being.

siva_et: 11.22 The Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, Visvedevas, the two Asvins, Maruts, the manes and the hosts of celestial singers, Yakshas, demons and the perfected ones, are all looking at Thee, in great amazement.
summary: All celestial beings and cosmic forces gaze upon the infinite form of the divine in sheer wonder and amazement.

siva_et: 11.23 Having seen Thy immeasurable form with many mouths and eyes, O mighty-armed, with many arms, thighs and feet, with many stomachs and fearful with many teeth  the worlds are terrified and so am I.
summary: Confronted with the overwhelming, boundless reality of the universe, the heart naturally trembles with fear and awe.

siva_et: 11.24 On seeing Thee (the Cosmic Form) touching the sky, shining in many colours, with mouths wide open, with large fiery eyes, I am terrified at heart and find neither courage nor peace, O Vishnu.
summary: When faced with forces far greater than ourselves, it is easy to lose our inner courage and peace completely.

siva_et: 11.25 Having seen Thy mouths fearful with teeth (blazing) like the fires of cosmic dissolution, I know not the four arters, nor do I find peace. Have mercy, O Lord of the gods, O abode of the universe.
summary: Overwhelmed by life's terrifying and destructive aspects, a person naturally seeks refuge, mercy, and calm from the Divine.

siva_et: 11.26 All the sons of Dhritarashtra, with the hosts of kings of the earth, Bhishma, Drona and Karna, with the chief among our warriors.
summary: All the powerful leaders, teachers, and loved ones on both sides of the battlefield are swept up in the march of time.

siva_et: 11.27 Some hurriedly enter Thy mouths with their terrible teeth, fearful to behold. Some are found sticking in the gaps between the teeth with their heads crushed to powder.
summary: A stark reminder of mortality, as lives are relentlessly drawn into the jaws of cosmic destruction and change.

siva_et: 11.28 Verily, just as many torrents of rivers flow towards the ocean, even so these heroes in the world of men enter Thy flaming mouths.
summary: Just as rivers naturally flow into the vast ocean, all worldly lives are inevitably drawn toward their final destination in time.

siva_et: 11.29 As moths hurriedly rush into a blazing fire for (their own) destruction, so also these creatures hurriedly rush into Thy mouths for (their own) destruction.
summary: Human beings often rush blindly toward their own undoing, caught up in the fierce and unstoppable currents of worldly existence.

siva_et: 11.30 Thou lickest up, devouring all the worlds on every side with Thy flaming mouths. Thy fierce rays, filling the whole world with radiance, are burning, O Vishnu!
summary: The consuming, fiery energy of time touches every corner of existence, absorbing all worlds into its blazing radiance.

siva_et: 11.31 Tell me, who Thou art, so fierce of form. Salutations to Thee, O God Supreme: have mercy. I desire to know Thee, the original Being. I know not indeed Thy working.
summary: When life feels overwhelming and fierce, we naturally plead for understanding, mercy, and a deeper connection to the ultimate truth.

siva_et: 11.32 The Blessed Lord said  I am the full-grown world-destroying Time, now engaged in destroying the worlds. Even without thee, none of the warriors arrayed in the hostile armies shall live.
summary: Time is the great equalizer that eventually dissolves all things, reminding us that outcomes are already set beyond our personal control.

siva_et: 11.33 Therefore, stand up and obtain fame. Coner the enemies and enjoy the unrivalled kingdom. Verily by Me have they been already slain; be thou a mere instrument, O Arjuna.
summary: Step up to your responsibilities with courage, knowing that the ultimate results belong to a higher power while you act as the instrument.

siva_et: 11.34 Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, Karna and other brave warriors  these are already slain by Me: do thou kill; be not distressed with fear; fight and thou shalt coner thy enemies in battle.
summary: Do not let fear paralyze you from doing what is right; trust in the greater plan and step up to fulfill your duty.

siva_et: 11.35 Sanjaya said  Having heard that speech of Lord Krishna, Arjuna, with joined palms, trembling, prostrating himself, again addressed Krishna, in a choked voice, bowing down, overwhelmed with fear.
summary: Overwhelmed by the terrifying cosmic vision of the Divine, Arjuna trembles with fear and bows in deep reverence.

siva_et: 11.36 Arjuna said  It is meet, O Krishna, that the world delights and rejoices in Thy praise; demons fly in fear to all arters and the hosts of the perfected ones bow to Thee.
summary: Arjuna acknowledges that the whole universe naturally rejoices in the Divine's glory, while fear drives away negativity.

siva_et: 11.37 And why should they not, O great Soul, bow to Thee Who art greater (than all else), the primal cause even of the Creator (Brahma), O Infinite Being, O Lord of the gods, O Abode of the universe; Thou art the imperishable, the Being, the non-being and That which is the supreme (that which is beyond the Being and the non-being).
summary: Recognizing the Divine as the ultimate source of everything, Arjuna praises the eternal power that holds all existence together.

siva_et: 11.38 Thou art the primal God, the ancient Purusha, the supreme refuge of this universe, the knower, the knowable and the supreme Abode. By Thee is the universe pervaded, O Being of infinite forms.
summary: The Divine is seen as the ancient, unchanging source and ultimate refuge of the entire universe, present in all things.

siva_et: 11.39 Thou art Vayu, Yama, Agni, Varuna, the moon, the Creator, and the great-grandfather. Salutations, salutations unto Thee, a thousand times, and again salutations, salutations unto Thee.
summary: Arjuna offers endless bows of gratitude to the Divine, recognizing that every force and element in the universe is simply a manifestation of God.

siva_et: 11.40 Salutations to Thee, in front and behind! Salutations to Thee on every side! O All!! Thou infinite in power and prowess, pervadest all; wherefore Thou art all.
summary: With infinite power pervading every direction, the Divine truly is everything that exists.

siva_et: 11.41 Whatever I have presumptuously said from carelessness or love, addressing Thee as O Krishna! O Yadava! O Friend! regarding Thee merely as a friend, unknowing of this, Thy greatness.
summary: Arjuna humbly asks for forgiveness for the times he casually treated the Supreme Lord as just an ordinary friend, unaware of His true greatness.

siva_et: 11.42 In whatever way I may have insulted Thee for the sake of fun, while at play, reposing, sitting or at meals, when alone (with Thee), O Krishna, or in company  that I implore Thee, immeasurable one, to forgive.
summary: Regretting any unintentional disrespect shown during everyday moments of play or rest, Arjuna asks the immeasurable Lord for grace and pardon.

siva_et: 11.43 Thou art the Father of this world, moving and unmoving. Thou art to be adored by this world, Thou, the greatest Guru; (for) none there exists who is eal to Thee; how then could there be another superior to Thee in the three worlds, O Being of unealled power?
summary: As the supreme teacher and father of the moving and unmoving world, nothing and no one can ever equal the power of the Divine.

siva_et:
11.44 Therefore, bowing down, prostrating my body, I crave Thy forgiveness, O adorable Lord. As a father forgives his son, a friend his (dear) friend, a lover his beloved, even so shouldst Thou 
forgive me, O God.
summary: Prostrating fully, Arjuna begs for patience and forgiveness from the Divine, just as a loving father, friend, or partner forgives those they hold dear.

siva_et: 11.45 I am delighted, having seen what has never been seen before; and yet my mind is distressed with fear. Show me that (previous) form only, O God; have mercy, O God of gods, O Abode of the universe.
summary: Though amazed to witness a sight never seen before, Arjuna's mind is still trembling with fear, and he gently asks to see a comforting form again.

siva_et: 11.46 I desire to see Thee as before, crowned, bearing a mace, with the discus in hand, in Thy former form only, having four arms, O thousand-armed, Cosmic Form (Being).
summary: Longing for a sense of gentle familiarity, Arjuna asks to see the peaceful, four-armed human-like form of the Lord once more.

siva_et: 11.47 The Blessed Lord said  O Arjuna, this Cosmic Form has graciously been shown to thee by Me by My own Yogic power; full of splendour, primeval, and infinite, this Cosmic Form of Mine has never been seen before by anyone other than thyself.
summary: The Lord reassures Arjuna that this breathtaking, infinite cosmic form was revealed to him purely out of divine grace and deep love.

siva_et: 11.48 Neither by the study of the Vedas and sacrifices, nor by gifts nor by rituals nor by severe austerities can I be seen in this form in the world of men by any other than thyself, O great hero of the Kurus (Arjuna).
summary: The Supreme Lord explains that this overwhelming cosmic vision cannot be attained through hard rituals, studies, or austerities alone, but only through profound devotion.

siva_et: 11.49 Be not afraid, nor bewildered on seeing such a teriible form of Mine as this; with thy fear dispelled and with a gladdened heart, now behold again this former form of Mine.
summary: When life feels overwhelming and terrifying, Krishna gently reminds you to let go of your fear and look for the comforting, familiar grace surrounding you.

siva_et: 11.50 Sanjaya said  Having thus spoken to Arjuna, Krishna again showed His own form and the great Soul (Krishna), assuming His gentle form, consoled him (Arjuna) who was terrified.
summary: Even when you are shaken to your core by life's intensity, a higher, loving presence is always there to calm your heart and restore your peace.

siva_et: 11.51 Arjuna said  Having seen this Thy gentle human form, O Krishna, now I am composed and am restored to my own nature.
summary: Seeing the gentle, loving side of the divine helps your scattered heart settle down and return to its natural state of calm.

siva_et: 11.52 The Blessed Lord said  Very hard indeed it is to see this form of Mine which thou hast seen. Even the gods are ever longing to behold it.
summary: Experiencing true divine comfort is a rare and precious gift that brings deep fulfillment to the soul.

siva_et: 11.53 Neither by the Vedas nor by austerity, nor by gift, nor by sacrifice can I be seen in this form as thou hast seen Me (so easily).
summary: You cannot earn deep spiritual truth simply through hard rituals or rigid practices; it comes through grace and openness.

siva_et: 11.54 But by single-minded devotion can I, of this Form, be known and seen in reality and also entered into, O Arjuna.
summary: Through pure, wholehearted devotion and love, you can truly know and deeply connect with the divine.

siva_et: 11.55 He who does all actions for Me, who looks upon Me as the Supreme, who is devoted to Me, who is free from attachment, who bears enmity towards no creature, he comes to Me, O Arjuna.
summary: When you dedicate your daily actions to a higher purpose, let go of selfish attachments, and hold no hatred in your heart, you naturally find your way home to peace.

siva_et: 12.1 Arjuna said  Those devotees who, ever steadfast, thus worship Thee and those also who worship the imperishable and the unmanifested  which of them are better versed in Yoga?
summary: It's natural to question the best path forward—whether to focus on an abstract concept of the divine or a personal, loving presence.

siva_et: 12.2 The Blessed Lord said  Those who, fixing their mind on Me, worship Me, ever steadfast and endowed with supreme faith, are the best in Yoga in My opinion.
summary: The most grounded and steady path is to anchor your heart and mind in a loving, personal connection with the divine.

siva_et: Swami Sivananda did not comment on this sloka
summary: This verse is a placeholder for reflection, reminding us to hold space for stillness when commentary is absent.

siva_et: 12.4 Having restrained all the senses, even-minded everywhere, intent on the welfare of all beings  verily they also come unto Me.
summary: By mastering your senses, staying even-minded through life's ups and downs, and genuinely wishing well for everyone, you naturally align with the divine.

siva_et: 12.5 Greater is their trouble whose minds are set on the unmanifested; for the goal; the unmanifested, is very hard for the embodied to reach.
summary: Trying to connect with an abstract, formless concept of life can be unnecessarily exhausting; having a tangible, loving focus makes the journey much gentler.

siva_et: 12.6 But to those who worship Me, renouncing all actions in Me, regarding Me as the supreme gaol, meditating on Me with single-minded Yoga.
summary: When you release the need to control every outcome and dedicate your actions to a higher love, your spiritual practice becomes steady and effortless.

siva_et: 12.7 To those whose minds are set on Me, O Arjuna, verily I become ere long the saviour out of the ocean of Samsara.
summary: When you keep your heart anchored in the divine, you will be swiftly rescued from the overwhelming ocean of worldly worries and sorrow.

siva_et: 12.8 Fix thy mind in Me only, thy intellect in Me, (then) thou shalt no doubt live in Me alone hereafter.
summary: When you anchor your mind and heart completely in the Divine, you naturally find a permanent home of peace and oneness.

siva_et: 12.9 If thou art unable to fix thy mind steadily on Me, then by the Yoga of constant practice do thou seek to reach Me, O Arjuna.
summary: If keeping your mind still feels too hard right now, don't give up—just gently practice turning your focus back to what matters, over and over.

siva_et: 12.10 If thou art unable to practise even this Abhyasa Yoga, be thou intent on doing actions for My sake; even by doing actions for My sake, thou shalt attain perfection.
summary: If even regular practice feels out of reach, simply dedicate your daily work and efforts to something higher, and you will still find fulfillment.

siva_et: 12.11 If thou art unable to do even this, then, resorting to union with Me, renounce the fruits of all actions with the self controlled.
summary: If keeping up with practices is too overwhelming, just focus on letting go of your attachment to the outcomes of your actions.

siva_et: 12.12 Better indeed is knowledge than practice; than knowledge meditation is better; than meditation the renunciation of the fruits of actions: peace immediately follows renunciation.
summary: Quiet wisdom beats endless effort, but true, immediate peace comes when you finally let go of needing a specific result from your work.

siva_et: 12.13 He who hates no creature, who is friendly and compassionate to all, who is free from attachment and egoism, balanced in pleasure and pain, and forgiving.
summary: True grace is found in being deeply kind to everyone, dropping your defenses and ego, and staying steady through both joy and pain.

siva_et: 12.14 Ever content, steady in meditation, self-controlled, possessed of firm conviction, with the mind and intellect dedicated to Me, he, My devtoee, is dear to Me.
summary: A peaceful, contented spirit who stays steady and dedicates their inner life to the Divine is truly cherished by God.

siva_et: 12.15 He by whom the world is not agitated and who cannot be agitated by the world, and who is freed from joy, anger, fear and anxiety  he is dear to Me.
summary: When you live in such a way that you don't disturb the world—and outside chaos can't shake your inner calm—you are truly free from anxiety and anger.

siva_et: 12.16 He who is free from wants, pure, expert, unconcerned, and free from pain, renouncing all undertakings or commencements  he who is (thus) devoted to Me, is dear to Me.
summary: There is a deep, quiet freedom in wanting less, letting go of constant striving, and resting in a peaceful, unbothered state of mind.

siva_et: 12.17 He who neither rejoices, nor hates, nor grieves, nor desires, renouncing good and evil, and who is full of devotion, is dear to Me.
summary: True peace comes when you stop oscillating between craving what you want and grieving what you've lost, resting instead in quiet devotion.

siva_et: Swami Sivananda did not comment on this sloka
summary: This verse was not commented on, but the flow continues on the path of inner steadiness and peace.

siva_et: 12.19 He to whom censure and praise are eal, who is silent, content with anything, homeless, of a steady mind, and full of devotion  that man is dear to Me.
summary: When praise and criticism roll off your back equally, and you are deeply content with whatever life brings, you carry a beautiful, steady grace.

siva_et: 12.20 They verily who follow this immortal Dharma (law or doctrine) as described above, endowed with faith, regarding Me as their supreme goal, they, the devotees, are exceedingly dear to Me.
summary: Those who live by this path of loving devotion, holding the Divine as their ultimate north star, are deeply dear to the heart of existence.

siva_et: 13.1 Arjuna said  I wish to learn about Nature (matter) and the Spirit (soul), the field and the knower of the field, knowledge and that which ought to be known, O Kesava.
summary: Arjuna's humble question invites us all to look deeper: what is this physical body we wear, and who is the conscious spirit experiencing it?

siva_et: 13.2 The Blessed Lord said  This body, O Arjuna, is called the field; he who knows it is called the knower of the field, by those who know of them.
summary: Your physical body and mind are just the temporary 'field' you experience, while the true you is the inner observer watching it all.

siva_et: 13.3 Do thou also know Me as the knower of the field in all fields, O Arjuna. Knowledge of both the field and the knower of the field is considered by Me to be ï1the ï1 knowledge.
summary: Remember that the same divine presence animating your life is also present in everyone else, connecting us all at the deepest level.

siva_et: 13.4 What the field is and of what nature, what are its modifications and whence it is and also who He is and what His powers are  hear all that from Me in brief.
summary: Take a moment to understand what your mind and body are made of, and recognize the higher power that sustains them both.

siva_et: 13.5 Sages have sung in many ways, in various distinctive chants and also in the suggestive words indicative of the Absolute, full of reasoning and decisive.
summary: Wise souls throughout time have pondered these deep truths through poetry, logic, and sacred song to help us find clarity.

siva_et: 13.6 The great elements, egoism, intellect, and also the Unmanifested Nature, the ten senses and one (mind), and the five objects of the senses.
summary: Your human experience is built from physical elements, your senses, your mind, and your ego working together.

siva_et: 13.7 Desire, hatred, pleasure, pain, the aggregate (the body), intelligence, fortitude  the field has thus been briefly described with its modifications.
summary: All of your shifting emotions—like desire, anger, joy, and pain—are simply temporary changes happening within your physical and mental field.

siva_et: 13.8 Humility, unpretentiousness, non-injury, forgiveness, uprightness, service of the teacher, purity, steadfastness, self-control.
summary: True strength comes from humility, kindness, forgiveness, and keeping a steady, disciplined grip on your inner self.

siva_et: 13.9 Indifference to the objects of the senses and also absence of egoism; perception of (or reflection on) the evil in birth, death, old age, sickness and pain.
summary: True wisdom means letting go of arrogance and recognizing the inevitable hardships of birth, aging, sickness, and pain so you can rise above them.

siva_et: 13.10 Non-attachment, non-identification of the Self with son, wife, home and the rest, and constant even-mindedness on the attainment of the desirable and the undesirable.
summary: Find your peace by loosening your grip on worldly attachments and staying gracefully balanced whether life brings you joy or sorrow.

siva_et: 13.11 Unswerving devotion unto Me by the Yoga of non-separation, resort to solitary places, distaste for the society of men.
summary: Turn your heart toward the divine with unwavering devotion, finding quiet moments of solitude to reconnect with what truly matters.

siva_et: 13.12 Constancy in Self-knowledge, perception of the end of true knowledge  this is declared to be knowledge, and what is opposed to it is ignorance.
summary: Commitment to knowing your true self is the highest wisdom; everything else that keeps you trapped in illusion is just noise.

siva_et: 13.13 I will declare that which has to be known, knowing which one attains to immortality, the beginningless supreme Brahman, called neither being nor non-being.
summary: I will reveal to you the timeless ultimate reality, knowing which you will transcend ordinary existence and touch true immortality.

siva_et: 13.14 With hands and feet everywhere, with eyes, heads and mouths everywhere, with ears everywhere, He exists in the worlds enveloping all.
summary: The divine presence fills the entire universe, seeing through every eye, hearing through every ear, and embracing all of existence.

siva_et: 13.15 Shining by the functions of all the senses, yet without the senses; unattached, yet supporting all; devoid of alities, yet their experiencer.
summary: The divine source shines through every sense while remaining untouched by them, supporting everything in the universe without ever being tied down.

siva_et: 13.16 Without and within (all) beings the unmoving and also the moving; because of Its subtlety, unknowable; and near and far away is That.
summary: The divine is present everywhere, both inside and outside of everything, moving and unmoving, staying too subtle for our ordinary eyes to easily catch.

siva_et: 13.17 And undivided, yet It exists as if divided in beings; It is to be known as the supporter of being; It devours and It generates.
summary: Even though life appears broken into separate pieces, the underlying reality holding everything together is one indivisible whole, constantly creating and dissolving forms.

siva_et: 13.18 That, the Light of all lights, is said to be beyond darkness: knowledge, the knowable and the goal of knowledge, seated in the hearts of all.
summary: The ultimate light of awareness shines deep within your own heart, guiding you past all darkness as the ultimate source of all knowledge.

siva_et: 13.19 Thus the field, as well as knowledge and the knowable have been briefly stated. My devotee, knowing this, enters into My Being.
summary: When you truly understand your body, your mind, and the deeper spirit within, you open your heart completely to the divine.

siva_et: 13.20 Know thou that Nature (matter) and the Spirit are both beginningless; and know also that all modifications and alities are born of Nature.
summary: Both the material world and your inner spirit have no beginning, but all the changing qualities and emotions you experience come directly from physical nature.

siva_et: 13.21 In the production of the effect and the cause, Nature (matter) is said to be the cause; in the experience of pleasure and pain, the soul is said to be the cause.
summary: The material world provides the raw machinery of life and action, while your inner consciousness is what actually feels the happiness and the hurt.

siva_et: 13.22 The soul seated in Nature experiences the alities born of Nature; attachment to the alities is the cause of its birth in good and evil wombs.
summary: When your true self gets entangled in worldly habits and desires, you trap yourself in endless cycles of emotional highs, lows, and painful struggles.

siva_et: 13.23 The Supreme Soul in this body is also called the spectator, the permitter, the supporter, the enjoyer, the great Lord and the Supreme Self.
summary: Deep within this physical body sits a silent witness—a peaceful presence that watches over everything you experience without ever losing its calm.

siva_et: 13.24 He who thus knows the Spirit and Matter together with the alities, in whatever condition he may be, he is not born again.
summary: When you finally wake up to the truth of how spirit and matter interact, you break free from the exhausting cycles of rebirth and struggle, no matter what your current situation looks like.

siva_et: 13.25 Some by meditation behold the Self in the self by the self, others by the Yoga of knowledge, and still others by the Yoga of action.
summary: People find their way to truth through different paths—some through deep meditation, some through clear understanding, and others through dedicated, selfless action.
