siva_et: 13.26 Others also, not knowing thus, worship, having heard of It from others; they, too, cross beyond death, regarding what they have heard as the Supreme refuge.
summary: Even those who don't know the deep philosophy can find peace simply by listening to wisdom and trusting it, safely crossing over the fear of mortality.

siva_et: 13.27 Wherever a being is born, whether unmoving or moving, know thou, O best of the Bharatas (Arjuna), that it is from the union between the field and its knower.
summary: Every single living creature that comes into this world is born from the sacred meeting of physical matter and inner consciousness.

siva_et: 13.28 He sees, who sees the Supreme Lord, existing eally in all beings, the unperishing within the perishing.
summary: True clarity means looking past temporary physical bodies to see the same timeless, indestructible divine presence living equally inside every single person.

siva_et: 13.29 Because he who sees the same Lord eally dwelling everywhere does not destroy the Self by the self; he goes to the highest goal.
summary: When you stop letting your mind isolate you from others and start seeing the same divine life everywhere, you protect your own soul and reach the highest state of peace.

siva_et: 13.30 He sees, who sees that all actions are performed by Nature alone and that the Self is actionless.
summary: When you realize that life's physical events are just nature turning, you can find a deep, untroubled stillness within yourself.

siva_et: 13.31 When a man sees the whole variety of beings as resting in the One, and spreading forth from That alone, he then becomes Brahman.
summary: When you start seeing the underlying oneness connecting every living being, you experience a profound sense of spiritual awakening.

siva_et: 13.32 Being without beginning and being devoid of (any) alities, the Supreme Self, imperishable, though dwelling in the body, O Arjuna, neither acts nor is tainted.
summary: Your true self is timeless and pure, remaining untouched and untainted no matter what physical challenges or changes you go through.

siva_et: 13.33 As the all-pervading ether is not tainted, because of its subtlety, so the Self seated everywhere in the body is not tainted.
summary: Just like space can never be dirtied by what floats through it, your deepest essence remains completely pure, no matter the chaos around you.

siva_et:
13.34 Just as the one sun illumines the whole world, so also the Lord of the field (Supreme Self) 
illumines the whole field, O Arjuna.
summary: Just as a single sun lights up the whole world, the divine spark within illuminates your entire life and experience.

siva_et: 13.35 They who, by the eye of knowledge, perceive the distinction between the field and its knower and also the liberation from the Nature of being, go to the Supreme.
summary: By learning to see the difference between your temporary body and your true spiritual self, you open the door to ultimate freedom.

siva_et: 14.1 The Blessed Lord said  I will again declare (to thee) that supreme knowledge, the best of all knowledge, having known which all the sages have gone to the supreme perfection after this life.
summary: Here is the highest wisdom of all—the understanding that has helped so many seekers find ultimate peace and fulfillment.

siva_et: 14.2 They who, having taken refuge in this knowledge, have attained to unity with Me, are neither born at the time of creation nor are they disturbed at the time of dissolution.
summary: Anchoring yourself in this deep wisdom brings a lasting peace that remains unshaken by life's major upheavals or fears of the unknown.

siva_et: 14.3 My womb is the great Brahma; in that I place the germ; thence, O Arjuna, is the birth of all beings.
summary: Everything in the universe is cradled in a vast, nurturing matrix of creation that gives rise to all living things.

siva_et: 14.4 Whatever forms are produced, O Arjuna, in any womb whatsoever, the great Brahma is their womb and I am the seed-giving father.
summary: No matter where life takes form or what shape it assumes, a universal source lovingly originates and sustains it all.

siva_et: 14.5 Purity, passion and inertia  these alities, O Arjuna, born of Nature, bind fast in the body, the embodied, the indestructible.
summary: We are often caught in different mental states—calmness, frantic striving, or sluggishness—that keep us feeling restricted and tied down.

siva_et: 14.6 Of these, Sattva, which from its stainlessness is luminous and healthy, binds by attachment to happiness and by attachment to knowledge, O sinless one.
summary: Even a bright, peaceful frame of mind can quietly trap you if you become too attached to feeling happy or knowing things.

siva_et: 14.7 Know thou Rajas to be of the nature of passion, the source of thirst (for sensual enjoyment) and attachment; it binds fast, O Arjuna, the embodied one by attachment to action.
summary: A restless, driven mindset is fueled by constant craving and endless ambition, which keeps you hooked on a treadmill of frantic action.

siva_et: 14.8 But know thou Tamas to be born of ignorance, deluding all embodied beings; it binds fast, O Arjuna, by heedlessness, indolence and sleep.
summary: Sluggishness and lethargy cloud your judgment, dragging you down into a fog of sleepiness, carelessness, and inaction.

siva_et: 14.9 Sattva attaches to happiness, Rajas to action, O Arjuna, while Tamas verily shrouding knowledge attaches to heedlessness.
summary: Different mental energies pull us in different directions: one draws us toward happiness and clarity, another toward frantic activity, and another toward dullness.

siva_et: 14.10 Now Sattva arises (prevails), O Arjuna, having overpowered Rajas and Tamas; nor Rajas, having overpowered Sattva and Tamas; and now Tamas, having overpowered Sattva and Rajas.
summary: Your mind's inner qualities are constantly shifting, with peace, hustle, and heaviness taking turns dominating your thoughts.

siva_et: 14.11 When through every gate (sense) in this body, the wisdom-light shines, then it may be known that Sattva is predominant.
summary: When your mind is clear, calm, and wise, you can tell that the pure, uplifting quality of sattva is taking charge within you.

siva_et: 14.12 Greed, activity, the undertaking of actions, restlessness, longing  these arise when Rajas is predominant, O Arjuna.
summary: When the restless energy of rajas takes over, you'll find yourself overwhelmed by intense cravings, endless striving, and constant agitation.

siva_et: 14.13 Darkness, inertness, heedlessness and delusion  these arise when Tamas is predominant, O Arjuna.
summary: When the heavy energy of tamas dominates, you might feel stuck in a fog of darkness, laziness, and confusion where nothing seems clear.

siva_et: 14.14 If the embodied one meets with death when Sattva is predominant, then he attains to the spotless worlds of the knowers of the Highest.
summary: If your mind is peaceful and clear at the time you pass away, you transition into higher, more luminous realms of awareness.

siva_et: 14.15 Meeting death in Rajas, he is born among those who are attached to action; and dying in Tamas, he is born in the womb of the senseless.
summary: The state of your mind at death shapes where you head next—either back into a life driven by endless striving or into unawakened confusion.

siva_et: 14.16 The fruit of good action, they say, is Sattvic and pure, verily the fruit of Rajas is pain, and ignorance is the fruit of Tamas.
summary: Living with clarity brings purity, but living driven purely by frantic ambition ultimately leads to pain, and ignorance leads nowhere good.

siva_et: 14.17 From Sattva arises knowledge, and greed from Rajas; heedlessness and delusion arise from Tamas, and also ignorance.
summary: True understanding grows from a clear mind, while greed stems from frantic energy, and confusion and blindness come from heaviness.

siva_et: 14.18 Those who are seated in Sattva go upwards; the Rajasic dwell in the middle; and the Tamasic, abiding in the function of the lowest Guna, go downwards.
summary: Your dominant mental habits shape your spiritual evolution, lifting you up, keeping you stuck in the middle, or dragging you down.

siva_et: 14.19 When the seer beholds no agent other than the Gunas and knows That which is higher than they, he attains to My Being.
summary: When you realize that your moods and thoughts are just shifting natural forces rather than the true 'you,' you step into a higher reality.

siva_et: 14.20 The embodied one having crossed beyond these three Gunas out of which the body is evolved, is freed from birth, death, decay and pain, and attains to immortality.
summary: By rising above the constant tug-of-war of your mind's fluctuating moods, you break free from suffering, aging, and death to experience timeless peace.

siva_et: 14.21 Arjuna said  What are the marks of him who has transcended the three alities, O Lord? What is his conduct and how does he go beyond these three alities?
summary: Arjuna asks how to spot someone who has truly mastered their shifting moods, and how they actually live and move beyond them.

siva_et: 14.22 The Blessed Lord said  When light, activity and delusion are present, he hates them not, nor does he long for them when they are absent.
summary: A truly wise person remains completely steady, neither hating difficult mental states when they arise nor clinging to pleasant ones when they fade.

siva_et: 14.23 He who, seated like one unconcerned, is not moved by the alities, and who, knowing that the alities are active, is self-centred and moves not.
summary: When you learn to observe life's changing moods without getting pulled into them, you can rest steady in your own center.

siva_et: 14.24 Who is the same in pleasure and pain, who dwells in the Self, to whom a clod of earth, stone and gold are alike, who is the same to the dear and the unfriendly, who is firm, and to whom censure and praise are as one.
summary: True peace comes from staying steady whether you're facing praise or blame, joy or pain, or even wealth and a simple stone.

siva_et: 14.25 Who is the same in honour and dishonour, the same to friend and foe, abandoning all undertakings  he is said to have transcended the alities.
summary: By letting go of constant striving and treating friends, foes, honor, and dishonor as the same, you rise above life's turbulent waves.

siva_et: 14.26 And he who serves Me with unswerving devotion, he, crossing beyond the alities, is fit for becoming Brahman.
summary: Through steady, unwavering devotion to the Divine, you can transcend the limits of nature and realize your highest spiritual potential.

siva_et: 14.27 For I am the abode of Brahman, the immortal and the immutable, of everlasting Dharma and of absolute bliss.
summary: Rest in the timeless divine presence, which is the ultimate home of absolute bliss, unchanging truth, and eternal peace.

siva_et: 15.1 The Blessed Lord said  They (the wise) speak of the indestructible peepul tree having its root above and branches below, whose leaves are the metres or hymns: he who knows it is a knower of the Vedas.
summary: This world is often compared to a complex, upside-down tree with its roots in the divine, reflecting a deep spiritual mystery.

siva_et: 15.2 Below and above spread its branches, nourished by the Gunas; sense-objects are its buds; and below, in the world of men, stretch forth the roots, originating action.
summary: Our worldly desires and actions branch out in every direction, driven by the energies of nature and our own senses.

siva_et: 15.3 Its form is not perceived here as such, neither its end nor its origin, nor its foundation nor resting place: having cut asunder this firmly rooted peepul tree with the strong axe of non-attachment.
summary: To find true freedom, you must use the sharp tool of non-attachment to cut down the deeply rooted illusions of worldly life.

siva_et: 15.4 Then That goal should be sought for, whither having gone none returns again. I seek refuge in that Primeval Purusha Whence streamed forth the ancient activity or energy.
summary: Seek that ultimate, eternal state of being from which there is no looking back, surrendering to the divine source of all energy.

siva_et: 15.5 Free from pride and delusion, victorious over the evil of attachment, dwelling constantly in the Self, their desires having completely turned away, freed from the pairs of opposites known as pleasure and pain, the undeluded reach the eternal goal.
summary: Free yourself from pride, false attachments, and the constant tug-of-war of pleasure and pain to finally reach your eternal home.

siva_et: 15.6 Neither doth the sun illumine there nor the moon, nor the fire; having gone thither they return not; that is My supreme abode.
summary: There is a supreme, self-illuminating divine realm of ultimate peace and joy from which no one needs to return.

siva_et: 15.7 An eternal portion of Myself having become a living soul in the world of life, draws to (itself) the (five) senses with the mind for the sixth, abiding in Nature.
summary: At your core, your true self is an eternal spark of the divine, experiencing this world through the lens of mind and senses.

siva_et: 15.8 When the Lord (as the individual soul) obtains a body and when He leaves it, He takes these and goes (with them) as the wind takes the scents from their seats (flowers, etc.).
summary: Just as the wind carries the fragrance of flowers, your inner soul carries its subtle mind and senses from one body to the next.

siva_et: 15.9 Presiding over the ear, the eye, touch, taste and smell, as well as the mind, it enjoys the objects of the senses.
summary: Using your senses and mind as instruments, your inner self gently navigates and experiences all the objects of the world around you.

siva_et: 15.10 The deluded do not see Him Who departs, stays and enjoys; but they who possess the eye of knowledge behold Him.
summary: When your mind is clouded, you miss the deeper presence of life all around and within you. Cultivating inner awareness helps you finally see the divine reality right in front of you.

siva_et: 15.11 The Yogins striving (for perfection) behold Him dwelling in the Self; but, the unrefined and unintelligent, even though striving, see Him not.
summary: Inner clarity doesn't happen by accident; it takes sincere inner work and self-discipline to truly perceive the divine within. Without that inner refinement, even hard effort can leave you feeling blind and disconnected.

siva_et: 15.12 That light which residing in the sun illumines the whole world, that which is in the moon and in the fire  know that light to be Mine.
summary: All the brilliance and beauty lighting up the universe—from the sun to the stars—come straight from the divine source. Recognizing this warmth around you can help you feel deeply cared for and connected.

siva_et: 15.13 Permeating the earth I support all beings by (My) energy; and having become the watery moon I nourish all herbs.
summary: The divine isn't distant; it is actively holding up the earth and sustaining all living things. You are completely supported by a loving, life-giving energy every moment of your day.

siva_et: 15.14 Having become the fire Vaisvanara, I abide in the body of living beings and, associated with the Prana and the Apana, digest the fourfold food.
summary: Even the everyday physical functions of your body, like your breath and your energy, are fueled by a sacred presence living right inside you. You are never truly running on empty, because a profound vitality beats at your core.

siva_et: 15.15 And I am seated in the hearts of all; from Me are memory and knowledge, as well as their absence. I am verily That which has to be known by all the Vedas; I am indeed the author of the Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas am I.
summary: The source of your memory, your insights, and your very consciousness lives quietly right inside your heart. No matter how lost you feel, that deep inner wisdom is always with you.

siva_et:
15.16 Two Purushas there are in this world, the perishable and the imperishable. All beings are 
the perishable and the Kutastha  the unchanging  is called the imperishable.
summary: Everything in this world is split between what constantly changes and fades away, and the quiet, unchanging essence underneath. Knowing the difference helps you stop clinging to things that cannot last.

siva_et: 15.17 But distinct is the Supreme Purusha called the highest Self, the indestructible Lord Who, pervading the three worlds, sustains them.
summary: Beyond everything temporary and fragile stands the supreme, indestructible presence that holds the entire universe together. Leaning on this ultimate reality can give you unshakeable ground when your world feels unstable.

siva_et: 15.18 As I transcend the perishable and am even higher than the imperishable, I am declared to be the highest Purusha in the world and in the Vedas.
summary: The divine reality is higher than both fleeting material things and static spiritual concepts. Recognizing this ultimate truth connects you to the deepest source of existence.

siva_et: 15.19 He who, undeluded, knows Me thus as the highest Purusha, he, knowing all, worships Me with his whole being (heart), O Arjuna.
summary: When you truly understand this supreme truth with your whole heart, everything else falls into place. That deep recognition naturally draws you into a life of complete devotion and peace.

siva_et: 15.20 Thus, this most secret science has been taught by Me, O sinless one; on knowing this, a man becomes wise, and all his duties are accomplished, O Arjuna.
summary: This profound understanding is the ultimate guide to waking up from confusion. Once you truly get it, your searching is complete and you can move forward with total clarity and confidence.

siva_et: 16.1 The Blessed Lord said  Fearlessness, purity of heart, steadfastness in knowledge and Yoga, almsgiving, control of the senses, sacrifice, study of scriptures, austerity and straightforwardness.
summary: Stepping onto a spiritual path starts with courage, honesty, and a willingness to let go of fear. Cultivating these noble qualities transforms your heart and anchors you in goodness.

siva_et: 16.2 Harmlessness, truth, absence of anger, renunciation, peacefulness, absence of crookedness, compassion towards beings, non-covetousness, gentleness, modesty, absence of fickleness.
summary: True strength looks like gentleness, compassion, and letting go of anger and greed. Choosing kindness and truthfulness every day heals both you and the world around you.

siva_et: 16.3 Vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, absence of hatred, absence of pride  these belong to the one born for a divine state, O Arjuna.
summary: Courage, forgiveness, and freedom from arrogance are the natural hallmarks of a noble, spiritually grounded soul. Letting go of your pride opens the door to genuine inner peace and strength.

siva_et: 16.4 Hypocrisy, arrogance and self-conceit, anger and also harshness and ignorance, belong to one who is born for a demoniacal state, O Partha (Arjuna).
summary: Hypocrisy, arrogance, anger, and harshness are traits that trap you in heavy, destructive habits. Recognizing these tendencies within yourself is the first step toward rising above them.

siva_et: 16.5 The divine nature is deemed conducive to liberation, and the demoniacal to bondage. Grieve not, O Arjuna, thou art born with divine endowments.
summary: Qualities rooted in truth and kindness lead you toward inner freedom, while harmful habits keep you bound. Do not despair or beat yourself up—you inherently carry goodness within you.

siva_et: 16.6 There are two types of beings in this world, the divine and the demoniacal; the divine has been described at length; hear from Me, O Arjuna, of the demoniacal.
summary: Human nature generally falls into two patterns: one that lifts us toward light and freedom, and another that pulls us into darkness. Understanding these two paths helps you consciously choose who you want to be.

siva_et: 16.7 The demoniacal know not what to do and what to refrain from; neither purity, nor right conduct nor truth is found in them.
summary: When people lose touch with their deeper values, they completely forget how to tell right from wrong. Without purity and truth, it becomes easy to lose your way in life.

siva_et: 16.8 They say, "This universe is without truth, without (moral) basis, without a God, brought about by mutual union, with lust for its cause; what else?"
summary: Some people view the universe as entirely random and meaningless, driven only by physical desires and survival. Living with this worldview strips life of its deeper purpose and wonder.

siva_et: 16.9 Holding this view, these ruined souls of small intellect and fierce deeds, come forth as the enemies of the world for its destruction.
summary: When people lose their moral compass, they become their own worst enemies and sources of harm to the world around them. Their small-minded focus ultimately leads to their own undoing.

siva_et: 16.10 Filled with insatiable desires, full of hypocrisy, pride and arrogance, holding evil ideas through delusion, they work with impure resolves.
summary: Being consumed by endless cravings, pride, and pretense clouds your judgment and poisons your intentions. When you act from this place, you only create more inner turmoil.

siva_et: 16.11 Giving themselves over to immeasurable cares ending only with death, regarding gratification of lust as their highest aim, and feeling sure that that is all.
summary: Getting trapped in endless worries and treating physical pleasure as the ultimate goal is a heavy, exhausting way to live. It leaves you constantly anxious about an uncertain future that ends in mortality.

siva_et: 16.12 Bound by a hundred ties of hope, given over to lust and anger, they strive to obtain by unlawful means hoards to wealth for sensual enjoyments.
summary: Being tangled in endless expectations, anger, and greed drives people to chase wealth by any means necessary just to feed their senses. This relentless pursuit keeps the mind in a state of constant agitation.

siva_et: 16.13 "This has been gained by me today; this desire of mine I shall fuffil; this is mine and this wealth also shall be mine in future."
summary: An ego-driven mindset constantly tallies up what has been won and plots how to grab more wealth and control. It's a restless cycle of saying 'this is mine' without ever finding true rest.

siva_et: 16.14 "That enemy has been slain by me; and others also I shall slay. I am the lord. I enjoy. I am perfect, powerful and happy."
summary: Arrogance whispers that you are the supreme master, invincible and entitled to dominate everyone else. This fierce need to conquer and enjoy at others' expense isolates you from genuine connection.

siva_et: 16.15 "I am rich and born in a noble family. Who else is equal to me? I shall perform sacrifices. I shall give (charity). I shall rejoice," thus deluded by ignorance.
summary: Pride in your wealth, status, and accomplishments can make you look down on everyone else. When you are caught in this illusion, even your acts of charity are tainted by ego.

siva_et: 16.16 Bewildered by many a fancy, entangled in the snare of delusion, addicted to the gratification of lust, they fall into a foul hell.
summary: Getting swept away by endless fantasies and chasing sensory pleasures eventually leads to deep emotional pain. Confusion and delusion always exact a heavy toll on your peace of mind.

siva_et: 16.17 Self-conceited, stubborn, filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform sacrifices in name out of ostentation, contrary to scriptural ordinances.
summary: When you are blinded by wealth and self-importance, even acts of service or devotion become empty shows for other people. True goodness doesn't need to put on a performance to feel worthy.

siva_et: 16.18 Given over to egoism, power, haughtiness, lust and anger, these malicious people hate Me in their own bodies and in those of others.
summary: When we let arrogance, greed, and anger take over, we end up hurting both ourselves and others.

siva_et: 16.19 Those cruel haters, worst among men in the world, I hurl those evil-doers into the wombs of demons only.
summary: Acting out of pure cruelty and malice only traps us deeper in cycles of pain and destructive habits.

siva_et: 16.20 Entering into demoniacal wombs and deluded, birth after birth, not attaining Me, they thus fall, O Arjuna, into a condition still lower than that.
summary: Being blinded by ego and delusion keeps us feeling lost and stuck, moving further away from inner peace.

siva_et: 16.21 Triple is the gate of this hell, destructive of the self  lust, anger and greed; therefore one should abandon these three.
summary: Lust, anger, and greed are the three destructive traps that rob us of our peace—let's make a conscious effort to let them go.

siva_et: 16.22 A man who is liberated from these three gates to darkness, O Arjuna, practises what is good for him and thus goes to the Supreme Goal.
summary: When you break free from destructive cravings and anger, you naturally find your way to a happier, more fulfilling life.

siva_et: 16.23 He who, having cast aside the ordinances of the scriptures, acts under the impulse of desire, attains not perfection, nor happiness nor the Supreme Goal.
summary: Just chasing temporary desires without any guidance or self-control will never lead you to true happiness or fulfillment.

siva_et: 16.24 Therefore, let the scripture be thy authority in determining what ought to be done and what ought not to be done. Having known what is said in the ordinance of the scriptures, thou shouldst act here in this world.
summary: Use timeless wisdom as your compass to figure out the right thing to do in difficult situations.

siva_et: 17.1 Arjuna said  Those who, setting aside the ordinances of the scriptures, perform sacrifice with faith, what is their condition, O Krishna? Is is Sattva, Rajas or Tamas?
summary: Arjuna asks about the fate of those who follow their own path with faith instead of strict rules—a question of where our heart's intentions truly lead us.

siva_et: 17.2 The Blessed Lord said  Threefold is the faith of the embodied, which is inherent in their nature  the Sattvic (pure), the Rajasic (passionate) and the Tamasic (dark). Do thou hear of it.
summary: The kind of faith we hold shapes our entire reality, falling into patterns of purity, passion, or darkness.

siva_et: 17.3 The faith of each is in accordance with his nature, O Arjuna. The man consists of his faith; as a man's faith is, so is he.
summary: You truly become what you deeply believe in; your faith is a mirror of your deepest self.

siva_et: 17.4 The Sattvic or the pure men worship the gods; the Rajasic or the passionate worship the Yakshas and the Rakshasas; the others (the Tamasic or the deluded people) worship the ghosts and the hosts of the nature-spirits.
summary: What we worship and value reflects our inner state of mind, whether it is pure, restless, or clouded.

siva_et: 17.5 Those men who practise terrific austerities not enjoined by the scriptures, given to hypocrisy and egoism, impelled by the force of lust and attachment.
summary: Pushing yourself to extreme limits driven only by ego, fake piety, and selfish desires only leads to burnout.

siva_et: 17.6 Senseless, torturing all the elements in the body and Me also, Who dwell in the body,  know thou these to be of demonical resolves.
summary: When you torture your mind and body with extreme, ego-driven habits, you drain your vitality and lose touch with your inner spirit.

siva_et: 17.7 The food also which is dear to each is threefold, as also sacrifice, austerity and almsgiving. Hear thou the distinction of these.
summary: Even the everyday choices we make—like what we eat or how we give—reflect our inner nature and state of mind.

siva_et: 17.8 The foods which increase life, purity, strength, health, joy and cheerfulness (good appetite), which are savoury and oleaginous, substantial and agreeable, are dear to the Sattvic (pure) people.
summary: Nourishing, wholesome food naturally brings vitality, clear health, and a cheerful spirit to your daily life.

siva_et: 17.9 The foods that are bitter, sour, saline, excessively hot, pungent, dry and burning, are liked by the Rajasic and are productive of pain, grief and disease.
summary: Heavy, overly spicy, or harsh foods tend to weigh down your body and mind, eventually leading to discomfort and distress.

siva_et: 17.10 That which is state, tasteless, putrid, rotten, refuse and impure, is the food liked by the Tamasic.
summary: Stale, lifeless, or impure foods drain your energy and cloud your mind, leaving you feeling sluggish and dull.

siva_et: 17.11 That sacrifice which is offered by men without desire for reward as enjoined by the ordinance (scripture), with a firm faith that to do so is a duty, is Sattvic or pure.
summary: When you simply do what is right because it is your duty, without clinging to any reward, your actions become pure and grounded.

siva_et: 17.12 The sacrifice which is offered, O Arjuna, seeking a reward and for ostentation, know thou that to be a Rajasic Yajna.
summary: Actions performed purely for show, applause, or personal gain stem from a restless desire for validation and status.

siva_et: 17.13 They declare that sacrifice to be Tamasic which is contrary to the ordinances of the scriptures, in which no food is distributed, which is devoid of Mantras, gifts and faith.
summary: Actions done carelessly, without genuine care, respect, or thoughtfulness, miss the mark and leave you feeling empty.

siva_et: 17.14 Worship of the gods, the twice-born, the teachers and the wise, purity, straightforwardness, celibacy and non-injury are called the austerities of the body.
summary: Treating others with respect, keeping your body clean, and living honestly form the foundational discipline of physical grace.

siva_et: 17.15 Speech which causes no excitement, truthful, pleasant and beneficial, the practice of the study of the Vedas, are called austerity of speech.
summary: Using your words kindly, truthfully, and helpfully creates peace instead of stirring up unnecessary drama.

siva_et: 17.16 Serenity of mind, good-heartedness, self-control, purity of nature  this is called mental austerity.
summary: Cultivating mental calm, kindness, self-control, and purity of thought brings a deep, steady peace to your inner world.

siva_et: 17.17 This threefold austerity, practised by steadfast men, with the utmost faith, desiring no reward, they call Sattvic.
summary: Practicing self-discipline and kindness with steady faith and zero expectation of personal reward transforms your character.

siva_et: 17.18 The austerity which is practised with the object of gaining good reception, honour and worship, and with hypocrisy, is here said to be Rajasic, unstable and transitory.
summary: Doing good deeds just to look impressive or win praise is fragile and fleeting, driven entirely by ego rather than heart.

siva_et: 17.19 That austerity which is practised out of a foolish notion, with self-torture, or for the purpose of destroying another, is declared to be Tamasic.
summary: Actions born from confusion, self-torture, or the desire to harm others only bring pain and misery to yourself and those around you.

siva_et: 17.20 That gift which is given to one who does nothing in return, knowing it to be a duty to give in a fit place and time to a worthy person, that gift is held to be Sattvic.
summary: True generosity means giving freely to support others simply because it is the right thing to do, expecting nothing back.

siva_et: 17.21 And, that gift which is given with a view to receive something in return, or looking for a reward, or reluctantly, is held to be Rajasic.
summary: Giving with reluctance or hoping for a future favor strips the act of its joy, turning it into a mere transaction.

siva_et: 17.22 The gift that is given at a wrong place and time, to unworthy persons, without respect or with insult is declared to be Tamasic.
summary: When we act carelessly, disrespectfully, or without mindfulness in how we treat others, our actions lack true goodness and awareness.

siva_et: 17.23 "Om Tat Sat": This has been declared to be the triple designation of Brahman. By that were created formerly, the Brahmanas, the Vedas and the sacrifices.
summary: The sacred syllables 'Om Tat Sat' represent the ultimate reality and the divine source from which everything in the universe was created.

siva_et: 17.24 Therefore, with the utterance of "Om" are the acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity as enjoined in the scriptures, always begun by the students of Brahman.
summary: Spiritual seekers begin their sacred acts, offerings, and disciplines by chanting 'Om' to align their efforts with the divine.

siva_et: 17.25 Uttering ï1Tatï1, without aiming at the fruits, are the acts of sacrifice and austerity and the various acts of gifts performed by the seekers of liberation.
summary: Those who seek true freedom perform their daily actions and charitable deeds without clinging to any personal rewards or outcomes.

siva_et: 17.26 The word ï1Satï1 is used in the sense of reality and of goodness; and so also, O Arjuna, the word ï1Satï1 is used in the sense of an auspicious act.
summary: The word 'Sat' is used to describe ultimate reality, supreme goodness, and any noble or auspicious action we take.

siva_et: 17.27 Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity and gift, is also called 'Sat' and also action in connection with these (or for the sake of the Supreme) is called 'Sat'.
summary: Steadfast commitment to acts of charity, self-discipline, and devotion is considered truly good and sacred when dedicated to the highest truth.

siva_et: 17.28 Whatever is sacrificed, given or performed, and whatever austerity is practised without faith, it is called 'Asat', O Arjuna; it is naught here or hereafter (after death).
summary: Whatever charity or discipline is done without genuine faith or heart holds no lasting value here or hereafter.

siva_et: 18.1 Arjuna said  I desire to know severally, O mighty-armed, the essence or truth of renunciation, O Hrishikesa, as also of abandonment, O slayer of Kesi.
summary: Arjuna asks Krishna to clearly explain the true meaning and difference between deep renunciation and letting go of results.

siva_et: 18.2 The Blessed Lord said  The sages understand Sannyasa to be the renunciation of action with desire; the wise declare the abandonment of the fruits of all actions as Tyaga.
summary: Wise ones understand that true renunciation means letting go of selfish desires and surrendering the personal fruits of your work.

siva_et: 18.3 Some philosophers declare that actions should be abandoned as an evil; while others (declare) that acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity should not be relinished.
summary: People are often confused, with some believing all actions should be stopped, while others argue that meaningful duties like charity and discipline must continue.

siva_et: 18.4 Hear from Me the conclusion or the final truth about this abandonment, O best of the Bharatas; abandonment, verily, O best of men, has been declared to be of three kinds.
summary: Krishna offers his definitive wisdom on the art of letting go, explaining that there are three distinct ways to practice abandonment.

siva_et: 18.5 Acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity should not be abandoned, but should be performed; sacrifice, gift and also austerity are the purifiers of the wise.
summary: Essential acts of service, charity, and self-discipline should never be given up; rather, they purify the mind and help us grow.

siva_et: 18.6 But even these actions should be performed leaving aside attachment and the desire for rewards, O Arjuna; this is My certain and best conviction.
summary: Even necessary duties should be performed freely, without clinging to personal rewards or agonizing over the outcomes.

siva_et: 18.7 Verily the renunciation of obligatory action is not proper; the abandonment of the same from delusion is declared to be Tamasic.
summary: Abandonding your daily responsibilities out of confusion, laziness, or emotional exhaustion is misguided and leads nowhere.

siva_et: 18.8 He who abandons action on account of the fear of bodily trouble (because it is painful), does not obtain the merit of renunciation by doing such Rajasic renunciation.
summary: Trying to escape your responsibilities simply because they feel physically or mentally exhausting doesn't count true letting go. True growth means facing what's in front of you rather than running away from discomfort.

siva_et: 18.9 Whatever obligatory action is done, O Arjuna, merely because it ought to be done, abandoning attachment and also the desire for reward, that renunciation is regarded as Sattvic (pure).
summary: When you do what you need to do simply because it is right, without clinging to praise or the outcome, you find a deep sense of peace. Let go of needing a reward for every little effort you make.

siva_et: 18.10 The man of renunciation, pervaded by purity, intelligent, and with his doubts cut asunder, does not hate a disagreeable work nor is he attached to an agreeable one.
summary: A clear, balanced mind doesn't resent the hard tasks or overly cling to the fun ones. When your doubts are cleared away, you can meet whatever comes your way with a steady heart.

siva_et: 18.11 Verily, it is not possible for an embodied being to abandon actions entirely; but he who relinishes the rewards of actions is verily called a man of renunciation.
summary: You can never completely stop being active in this life, but you *can* change your relationship to your work. Real freedom comes from releasing your obsession with the results of what you do.

siva_et: 18.12 The threefold fruit of action (evil, good and mixed) accrues after death to the non-abandoners, but never to the abandoners.
summary: People who constantly chase personal rewards and cling to outcomes inevitably get tangled up in the consequences of their actions over time. By letting go of that frantic grip, you free yourself from that heavy cycle.

siva_et: 18.13 Learn from Me, O mighty-armed Arjuna, these five causes as declared in the Sankhya system for the accomplishment of all actions.
summary: Let's look at how things actually get done in this world so you can understand your place in it. Wisdom helps us see the mechanics behind our efforts instead of feeling lost.

siva_et: 18.14 The seat (body), the doer, the various senses, the different functions of various sorts, and the presiding deity, also, the fifth.
summary: Every action relies on a combination of things: your physical body, your personality, your senses, your mental energy, and deeper universal forces. Recognizing these pieces helps you see you are part of something much bigger.

siva_et: 18.15 Whatever action a man performs with his body, speech and mind  whether right or the reverse  these five are its causes.
summary: Whether you are speaking, thinking, or moving through the world, everything you do is a collaborative effort of these deep natural forces. Understanding this helps take the heavy burden off your shoulders.

siva_et: 18.16 Now, such being the case, verily he who  owing to untrained understanding  looks upon his Self, which is isolated, as the agent, he of perverted intelligence, sees not.
summary: When you mistakenly believe that your small, limited self is the sole doer of everything, you trap yourself in confusion. True clarity sees beyond this illusion.

siva_et:
18.17 He who is free from the egoistic notion, whose intelligence is not tainted (by good or evil), 
though he slays these people, he slayeth not, nor is he bound (by the action).
summary: When your ego dissolves and you no longer act out of personal pride or malice, you are truly free. Even in hard situations, your spirit remains untainted and at peace.

siva_et: 18.18 Knowledge, the knowable and the knower form the threefold impulse to action; the organ, the action and the agent form the threefold basis of action.
summary: Every meaningful action starts with knowledge, an objective, and an actor, and is carried out through your tools and efforts. Understanding this structure helps you bring mindfulness to your daily life.

siva_et: 18.19 Knowledge, action and actor are declared in the science of the Gunas (Sankhya philosophy) to be of three kinds only, according to the distinction of the Gunas. Of these also, hear duly.
summary: Knowledge, action, and motivation all wear different flavors depending on the energy of your mind. Learning to recognize these patterns helps you understand why you feel and act the way you do.

siva_et: 18.20 That by which one sees the one indestructible Reality in all beings, not separate in all the separate beings  know thou that knowledge to be Sattvic.
summary: The highest kind of vision is being able to look past surface differences and see the same underlying spark of life in everyone. That deep connection brings a profound sense of inner calm.

siva_et: 18.21 But that knowledge which sees in all beings various entities of distinct kinds as different from one another  know thou that knowledge to be Rajasic.
summary: A fragmented or narrow view of the world keeps you trapped in division, seeing everything and everyone as separate and threatening. True clarity unites us, while a clouded mind constantly seeks conflict.

siva_et: 18.22 But that which clings to one single effect as if it were the whole, without reason, without foundation in Truth, and trivial  that is declared to be Tamasic.
summary: Holding blindly onto a narrow, irrational view of life without seeing the bigger truth keeps you trapped in darkness.

siva_et: 18.23 An action which is ordained, which is free from attachment, and which is done without love or hatred by one who is not desirous of any reward  that action is declared to be Sattvic.
summary: When you do what's required of you purely and selflessly, without obsessing over the outcome, your actions bring genuine peace.

siva_et: 18.24 But that action which is done by one longing for the fulfilment of desires or gain with egoism or with much effort  that is declared to be Rajasic (passionate).
summary: Pushing yourself to the limit simply out of greed, personal gain, or ego will only leave you stressed and restless.

siva_et: 18.25 That action which is undertaken from delusion, without a regard for the conseences, loss, injury and (one's own) ability  that is declared to be Tamasic (dark).
summary: Acting recklessly out of confusion, without considering the consequences or your own capacity, leads to unnecessary harm.

siva_et: 18.26 An agent who is free from attachment, non-egoistic, endowed with firmness and enthusiasm, and unaffected by success or failure, is called Sattvic (pure).
summary: True strength means staying steady, enthusiastic, and humble, completely unshakeable whether things go right or wrong.

siva_et: 18.27 Passionate, desiring to obtain the reward of actions, greedy, cruel, impure, moved by joy and sorrow, such an agent is said to be Rajasic (passionate).
summary: Being driven purely by greed, reward, and emotional volatility makes it hard to find peace.

siva_et: 18.28 Unsteady, vulgar, unbending, cheating, malicious, lazy, desponding and procrastinating  such an agent is called Tamasic.
summary: Feeling constantly lazy, unmotivated, discouraged, or scattered is a heavy, sluggish state of mind that holds you back.

siva_et: 18.29 Hear thou the threefold division of intellect and firmness according to the Gunas, as I declare them fully and distinctly, O Arjuna.
summary: Listen closely as we break down how your intellect and focus shape your everyday choices.

siva_et: 18.30 The intellect which knows the path of work and renunciation, what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, fear and fearlessness, bondage and liberation  that intellect is Sattvic (pure), O Arjuna.
summary: A clear, healthy mind easily recognizes what is right to do, what brings freedom, and what to steer clear of.

siva_et: 18.31 That, by which one wrongly understands Dharma and Adharma and also what ought to be done and what ought not to be done  that intellect, O Arjuna, is Rajasic (passionate).
summary: Sometimes your judgment gets clouded, making it hard to clearly tell right from wrong.

siva_et: 18.32 That, which, enveloped in darkness, sees Adharma as Dharma and all things perverted  that intellect, O Arjuna, is Tamasic (dark).
summary: When your mind is deeply clouded, you might start seeing harmful things as good and backwards things as truth.

siva_et: 18.33 The unwavering firmness by which, through Yoga, the functions of the mind, the life-force and the senses are restrained  that firmness, O Arjuna, is Sattvic (pure).
summary: Cultivating a steady, unwavering focus helps you naturally master your restless mind and senses.

siva_et: 18.34 But that, O Arjuna, by which, on account of attachment and desire for reward, one holds fast to Dharma (duty), enjoyment of pleasures and earning of wealth  that firmness, O Arjuna, is Rajasic (passionate).
summary: Holding onto your responsibilities only because you want a reward, wealth, or pleasure keeps you bound to constant craving.

siva_et: 18.35 That, by which a stupid man does not abandon sleep, fear, grief, despair and also conceit  that firmness, O Arjuna, is Tamasic.
summary: An unhealed, heavy mind stubbornly clings to fear, grief, despair, sleep, and pride, refusing to let them go.

siva_et: 18.36 And now hear from Me, O Arjuna, of the threefold pleasure, in which one rejoices by practice and surely comes to the end of pain.
summary: True happiness takes practice to cultivate, but stick with it—it's the path that ultimately leads you out of suffering.

siva_et: 18.37 That which is like poison at first but in the end like nectar  that happiness is declared to be Sattvic, born of the purity of one's own mind due to Self-realisation.
summary: The most deeply rewarding things in life often feel difficult or uncomfortable at first, but they lead to lasting peace and joy.

siva_et: 18.38 That happiness which arises from the contact of the sense-organs with the objects, which is at first like nectar, and in the end like poison  that is declared to be Rajasic.
summary: Quick fixes and instant gratification feel sweet in the moment, but chasing them always ends up causing pain and regret.

siva_et: 18.39 That happiness which at first as well as in the seel deludes the self, and which arises from sleep, indolence and heedlessness  that is declared to be Tamasic.
summary: Numbing out through laziness, sleep, or carelessness might feel easy right now, but it only keeps you stuck and confused.

siva_et: 18.40 There is no being on earth or again in heaven among the gods, that is liberated from the three alities born of Nature.
summary: Everyone in this universe experiences the pull of different emotional and mental states; you aren't alone in feeling tossed around by life.

siva_et: 18.41 Of Brahmanas, Kshatriyas and Vaisyas, as also of Sudras, O Arjuna, the duties are distributed according to the alities born of their own nature.
summary: We all have natural inclinations and roles in life that shape what we are meant to do and how we contribute.

siva_et: 18.42 Serenity, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forgiveness and also uprightness, knowledge, realisation and belief in God are the duties of the Brahmanas, born of (their own) nature.
summary: Developing qualities like patience, kindness, self-control, and a steady mind is part of living a meaningful and grounded life.

siva_et: 18.43 Prowess, splendour, firmness, dexterity and also not fleeing from battle, generosity and lordliness are the duties of the Kshatriyas, born of (their own) nature.
summary: Standing your ground with courage, strength, and generosity when challenges arise is a natural expression of a brave heart.

siva_et: 18.44 Agriculture, cattle-rearing and trade are the duties of the Vaisya (merchant), born of (their own) nature; and action consisting of service is the duty of the Sudra (servant-class), born of (their own) nature.
summary: Whether through honest work, commerce, or service to others, doing your daily labor with care is a valid and honorable path.

siva_et: 5.10 He who does actions, offering them to Brahman, and abandoning attachment, is not tainted by sin, just as a lotus-leaf is not tainted by water.
summary: When you let go of needing a specific outcome and offer your efforts to something greater, you stay completely untouched by stress and worry.

siva_et: 18.46 He from Whom all the beings have evolved and by Whom all this is pervaded  worshipping Him with his own duty, man attains perfection.
summary: You can find fulfillment and wholeness simply by showing up and offering your everyday work and responsibilities as an act of devotion.

siva_et: 18.47 Better is one's own duty (though) destitute of merits, than the duty of another well performed. He who does the duty ordained by his own nature incurs no sin.
summary: It's always better to fully embrace your own unique path and responsibilities—even if they feel messy—than to try to live someone else's life.

siva_et: 18.48 One should not abandon, O Arjuna, the duty to which one is born, though faulty; for, all undertakings are enveloped by evil, as fire by smoke.
summary: Don't abandon your responsibilities just because they feel flawed or difficult; every path in life comes with its own set of challenges.

siva_et: 18.49 He whose intellect is unattached everywhere, who has subdued his self, from whom desire has fled,  he by renunciation, attains the supreme state of freedom from action.
summary: When your mind is truly unattached, calm, and free from selfish craving, you reach a state of profound inner freedom and peace.

siva_et: 18.50 Learn from Me in brief, O Arjuna, how he who has attained perfection reaches Brahman (the Eternal), that supreme state of knowledge.
summary: Listen as I briefly explain how someone who reaches ultimate perfection attains the supreme state of the Divine.

siva_et: 18.51 Endowed with a pure intellect, controlling the self by firmness, relinishing sound and other objects and abandoning attraction and hatred.
summary: Purify your intellect, steady your mind with firmness, and let go of chasing sensory pleasures, attraction, and aversion.

siva_et: 18.52 Dwelling in solitude, eating but little, with speech, body and mind subdued, always engaged in meditation and concentration, resorting to dispassion.
summary: Find peace in solitude, eat moderately, master your body and mind, and keep your heart anchored in deep meditation and dispassion.

siva_et: 18.53 Having abandoned egoism, strength, arrogance, desire, anger and covetousness, and free from the notion of 'mine' and peaceful,  he is fit for becoming Brahman.
summary: Let go of pride, arrogance, desire, anger, and the need to possess things, and you will step into a deep, lasting peace.

siva_et: 18.54 Becoming Brahman, serene in the Self, he neither grieves nor desires, the same to all beings, he obtains supreme devotion to Me.
summary: When you are truly settled in your higher self, you stop grieving and craving, seeing all beings with an equal heart.

siva_et: 18.55 By devotion he knows Me in truth, what and who I am; then having known Me in truth, he forthwith enters into the Supreme.
summary: Through wholehearted devotion, you come to truly know who I am, and in that deep understanding, you merge into the infinite.

siva_et: 18.56 Doing all actions always having taken refuge in Me, by My grace he obtains the eternal indestructible state of being.
summary: By dedicating all your actions to Me and taking refuge in My grace, you will attain an eternal, indestructible state of being.

siva_et: 18.57 Mentally renouncing all actions in Me, having Me as the highest goal, resorting to the Yoga of discrimination do thou ever fix thy mind on Me.
summary: Mentally offer all your actions up to Me, make Me your highest goal, and keep your mind steadily focused on My presence.

siva_et: 18.58 Fixing thy mind on Me, thou shalt by My grace overcome all obstacles; but if from egoism thou wilt not hear Me, thou shalt perish.
summary: Fix your mind on Me and you will safely navigate every obstacle through My grace, but if you let your ego blind you, you will stumble.

siva_et: 18.59 If, filled with egoism, thou thinkest: "I will not fight", vain is this, thy resolve; Nature will compel thee.
summary: If you let your ego drive you to say 'I will not fight this battle,' your resistance is pointless; your own inner nature will push you forward anyway.

siva_et: 18.60 O Arjuna, bound by thy own Karma (action) born of thy own nature, that which from delusion thou wishest not to do, even that thou shalt do helplessly.
summary: Bound by the habits of your own nature and past actions, you will end up doing effortlessly what you were resisting out of confusion.

siva_et: 18.61 The Lord dwells in the hearts of all beings, O Arjuna, causing all beings, by His illusive power, to revolve as if mounted on a machine.
summary: The Divine dwells within the heart of every single being, guiding our journey as if we are riding on the machinery of life.

siva_et: 18.62 Fly unto Him for refuge with all thy being, O Arjuna; by His grace thou shalt obtain supreme peace (and) the eternal abode.
summary: Surrender completely to the Divine with all your heart, and through that grace, you will find ultimate peace and an eternal home.

siva_et: 18.63 Thus has wisdom, more secret than secrecy itself, been declared unto thee by Me; having reflected over it fully, then act as thou wishest.
summary: I have shared this deepest wisdom with you; now ponder it carefully in your heart, and then freely choose what you wish to do.

siva_et: 18.64 Hear thou again My supreme word, most secret of all; because thou art dearly beloved of Me, I will tell thee what is good.
summary: Krishna shares a final, deeply loving truth meant to uplift and guide you through life's toughest moments.

siva_et: 18.65 Fix thy mind on Me, by devoted to Me, sacrifice to Me, bow down to Me. Thou shalt come even to Me; truly do I promise unto thee, (for) thou art dear to Me.
summary: When you anchor your heart completely in the divine and let go of anxiety, you find a deep, unshakable peace.

siva_et: 18.66 Abandoning all duties, take refuge in Me alone: I will liberate thee from all sins; grieve not.
summary: Stop carrying the heavy burden of all your worries and expectations; surrender them entirely, and you will be freed from sorrow.

siva_et: 18.67 This is never to be spoken by thee to one who is devoid of austerities or devotion, nor to one who does not render service or who does not desire to listen, nor to one who cavils at Me.
summary: Keep your most sacred insights and vulnerable truths protected, sharing them only with those who are truly ready to receive them with an open heart.

siva_et: 18.68 He who with supreme devotion to Me will teach this supreme secret to My devotees, shall doubtlessly come to Me.
summary: Sharing the wisdom of love and devotion with others is a profound gift that naturally brings you closer to peace.

siva_et: 18.69 Nor is there any among men who does dearer service to Me, nor shall there be another on earth dearer to Me than he.
summary: There is nothing more dear to the universe than a heart that spreads kindness, love, and spiritual truth.

siva_et: 18.70 And he who will study this sacred dialogue of ours, by him I shall have been worshipped by the sacrifice of wisdom,  such is My conviction.
summary: Taking the time to study and reflect on timeless wisdom is a powerful offering of self-improvement and devotion.

siva_et: 18.71 Also the man who hears this, full of faith and free from malice, he, too, liberated, shall attain to the happy worlds of those of righteous deeds.
summary: Approaching life's teachings with an open mind and a kind heart helps lift the heavy burdens of the past, leading you toward freedom.

siva_et: 18.72 Has this been heard, O Arjuna, with one-pointed mind? Has the delusion of thy ignorance been destroyed, O Dhananjaya?
summary: Take a moment to check in with yourself: have you finally started to see past the confusion and fog that was clouding your judgment?

siva_et: 18.73 Arjuna said  Destroyed is my delusion as I have gained my knowledge (memory) through Thy grace, O Krishna. I remain freed from doubts. I will act according to Thy word.
summary: The fog has lifted, your confusion is gone, and you finally feel clear enough to step forward and do what needs to be done.

siva_et: 18.74 Sanjaya said  Thus I have heard this wonderful dialogue between Krishna and the high-souled Arjuna, which causes the hair to stand on end.
summary: Listening to the deep dialogue of truth within yourself can stir your soul and awaken a profound sense of wonder.

siva_et: 18.75 Through the grace of Vyasa I have heard this supreme and most secret Yoga direct from Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, Himself declaring it.
summary: Through grace, we are given direct access to the wisdom that can heal our deepest struggles.

siva_et: 18.76 O King, remembering this wonderful and holy dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.
summary: Whenever you pause to remember life's deepest truths, a quiet joy and reassurance wash over you.

siva_et: 18.77 And, remembering again and again, also that most wonderful form of Hari, great is my wonder, O King; and I rejoice again and again.
summary: Reflecting on the vast, beautiful mystery of life fills your heart with endless wonder and quiet happiness.

siva_et: 18.78 Wherever is Krishna, the Lord of Yoga; wherever is Arjuna, the wielder of the bow; there are prosperity, victory, happiness and firm policy; such is my conviction.
summary: Wherever divine wisdom and sincere effort unite, you will ultimately find lasting peace, clarity, and success. Trust that you are never walking your path alone.
